ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَوْفُوا بِالْعُقُودِ أُحِلَّتْ لَكُمْ بَهِيمَةُ الْأَنْعَامِ إِلَّا مَا يُتْلَى عَلَيْكُمْ غَيْرَ مُحِلِّي الصَّيْدِ وَأَنْتُمْ حُرُمٌ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَحْكُمُ مَا يُرِيدُ) (١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا مَا يُتْلَى عَلَيْكُمْ): in the position of the accusative (naṣb) as an exception from «بَهِيمَةِ الْأَنْعَامِ», and the exception is connected (muttaṣil). The implied form is: "the beast of cattle is made lawful for you except carrion, and what has been dedicated to other than Allah, and the rest of what is mentioned in the third verse of the sūra". (غَيْرَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the genitive pronoun in عليكم or لكم; it has also been said that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun of the fāʿil (agent) in أوفوا. And (مُحِلِّي): an active participle annexed to its object, the nūn having been dropped for the annexation (iḍāfa). And (الصَّيْدِ): a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of the object, that is, [in the sense of] the game «[Translator's note: the printed text reads أي المصدر "that is, the maṣdar", which seems to be a slip for أي المَصِيد "that is, the game"; translated according to the evident sense.]». It may also be [a maṣdar] in its proper sense here, that is: not making hunting lawful while in the state of iḥrām.

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تُحِلُّوا شَعَائِرَ اللَّهِ وَلَا الشَّهْرَ الْحَرَامَ وَلَا الْهَدْيَ وَلَا الْقَلَائِدَ وَلَا آمِّينَ الْبَيْتَ الْحَرَامَ يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَرِضْوَانًا وَإِذَا حَلَلْتُمْ فَاصْطَادُوا وَلَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَآنُ قَوْمٍ أَنْ صَدُّوكُمْ عَنِ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ أَنْ تَعْتَدُوا وَتَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الْبِرِّ وَالتَّقْوَى وَلَا تَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوَانِ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ) (٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَا الْقَلَائِدَ): that is, nor those wearing garlands (ذوات القلائد), because it is the plural of قلادة (garland), and what is meant is the prohibition [of violating] the garlanded animal, not the garland. (وَلَا آمِّينَ): that is, nor fighting those heading [for the House], or harming those heading [for it]. In an irregular (shādhdh) reading it has been read: «وَلَا آمِّي الْبَيْتِ», with the nūn dropped and annexation.
(يَبْتَغُونَ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in آمّين. It may not be an adjective (ṣifa) of آمّين, because when an active participle is qualified by an adjective it does not govern, in the chosen usage. (فَاصْطَادُوا): it has been read in an irregular reading with kasra on the fāʾ, and this is far from correct; it is as if he gave it the vowel of the connecting hamza. (وَلَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ): the majority read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ, and it has been read with ḍamma; they are two dialectal forms: one says جَرَمَ and أَجْرَمَ. It has also been said that جرم is transitive to one object and أجرم transitive to two, the hamza being for transfer (naql). As for the fāʿil (agent) of this verb, it is «شَنَآنُ», and its first object is the kāf and mīm. And (أَنْ تَعْتَدُوا): it is the second object on the view of those who make it transitive to two objects; those who make it transitive to one as it were take a preposition to be intended with «أَنْ تَعْتَدُوا». The meaning is: let not hatred of a people drive you to transgression. The majority read the first nūn of شنآن with fatḥa, and it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) like الغليان and النزوان; and it is read with sukūn on it, and then it is an adjective like عطشان and سكران, the implied form on this view being: let not [one] hateful of a people drive you, that is, the enmity of [one] hateful of a people «[Translator's note: the text repeats بغض قوم here; on the sukūn reading شنآن is an adjective "one who hates", which is how it is rendered.]». It has also been said: whoever reads it with sukūn also intends the maṣdar, but it has been lightened because of the number of vowels. When the nūn is vowelled, it is a maṣdar annexed to the object, that is: let not your hatred of a people drive you; and it may be annexed to the subject, that is: a people's hatred of you. (أَنْ صَدُّوكُمْ): it is read with fatḥa on the hamza, and then it is maṣdariyya, the implied form being: "because they barred you", and its position is accusative, or genitive, according to the disagreement over similar cases. And it is read with kasra on it, as a condition, and the meaning is: if they bar you with the like of that barring which occurred from them, or if they continue the barring. It was only construed thus because the barring had already occurred from the unbelievers against the Muslims. (وَلَا تَعَاوَنُوا): it is read with the two tāʾs lightened, on the basis that the second tāʾ was dropped for lightness, or with it doubled when you join it to لا, by assimilating one of the two tāʾs into the other; and the combination of two quiescent letters is permissible because the first of them is a letter of prolongation.

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَيْتَةُ وَالدَّمُ وَلَحْمُ الْخِنْزِيرِ وَمَا أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ وَالْمُنْخَنِقَةُ وَالْمَوْقُوذَةُ وَالْمُتَرَدِّيَةُ وَالنَّطِيحَةُ وَمَا أَكَلَ السَّبُعُ إِلَّا مَا ذَكَّيْتُمْ وَمَا ذُبِحَ عَلَى النُّصُبِ وَأَنْ تَسْتَقْسِمُوا بِالْأَزْلَامِ ذَلِكُمْ فِسْقٌ الْيَوْمَ يَئِسَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ دِينِكُمْ فَلَا تَخْشَوْهُمْ وَاخْشَوْنِ الْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِي وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ الْإِسْلَامَ دِينًا فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ فِي مَخْمَصَةٍ غَيْرَ مُتَجَانِفٍ لِإِثْمٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) (٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الْمَيْتَةُ): its original form is الميّتة. (وَالدَّمُ): its original form is دَمَى.
(وَمَا أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ): all of this has been mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Baqara.
(وَالنَّطِيحَةُ): in the sense of المنطوحة (the one gored). The hāʾ [of the feminine] has entered it because the qualified noun is not mentioned with it, so it has become like a noun; if you say شاة نطيح ("a gored ewe"), the hāʾ does not enter.
(وَمَا أَكَلَ السَّبُعُ): «مَا» is in the sense of الذي (relative noun), and its position is nominative (rafʿ), conjoined to الميتة. Most [read] the bāʾ of السبع with ḍamma; making it quiescent is a dialectal form, and it has been read so.
(إِلَّا مَا ذَكَّيْتُمْ): in the position of the accusative (naṣb) as an exception from the affirmative [statement] before it, and the exception goes back to the animal that fell (المتردية), the gored one (النطيحة) and the one eaten by a beast of prey.
(وَمَا ذُبِحَ): like «وَمَا أَكَلَ السَّبُعُ».
(عَلَى النُّصُبِ): there are two views on it. The first: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to ذُبح in the way an object is attached to the verb, that is: slaughtered on the stones that are called نُصُب, that is, slaughtered in that place. The second: that النصب are the idols; on this view «فِي» «[Translator's note: so in the text; the preposition under discussion is على.]» has two views. The first: it is in the sense of the lām, that is: for the sake of the idols, so it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). The second: that it is in its original sense and its position is a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is: and what was slaughtered with [the name of] the idols pronounced over it. And it has been said: نُصُب with two ḍammas, and نُصْب with ḍamma on the nūn and sukūn on the ṣād, and نَصْب with fatḥa on the nūn and sukūn on the ṣād, which is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of the object.
It has also been said that fatḥa on both the nūn and the ṣād is permissible, and it is a noun in the sense of المنصوب (that which is set up), like القَبَض and النَّقَض in the sense of المقبوض and المنقوض. (وَأَنْ تَسْتَقْسِمُوا): in the position of the nominative, conjoined to الميتة. And (الْأَزْلَامُ): the plural of زَلَم, which is the arrow with which they used to cast lots over the portions of the slaughtered camel. (ذَلِكُمْ فِسْقٌ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); and لكم «[Translator's note: so in the text; evidently ذلكم is meant.]» is a reference to all the prohibited things in the verse, and it may refer back to the seeking of lots (الاستقسام). (الْيَوْمَ): an adverb (ẓarf) of «يَئِسَ», and the second (الْيَوْمَ) is an adverb of «أَكْمَلْتُ». And (عَلَيْكُمُ) is attached to أتممت and is not attached to نعمتي; if you wish, you may take it as explanation (tabyīn), that is: I have completed — I mean, upon you. And (رَضِيتُ) is transitive to a single object, which here is «الْإِسْلَامُ».
And (دِينًا) is a ḥāl. It has also been said that it is transitive to two objects, because the meaning of رضيت here is "I made" and "I rendered". And لكم is attached to رضيت, and it is for specification (takhṣīṣ); and it may be a ḥāl from الإسلام, that is: I have approved Islam for you. (فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ): a condition in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and (غَيْرَ) is a ḥāl.
The majority read «مُتَجَانِفٍ» with the alif and without doubling, and it has been read «مُتَجَنِّفٍ», with doubling and without alif; one says تجانف and تجنّف. (لِإِثْمٍ): attached to متجانف. It has also been said that the lām is in the sense of إلى, that is: inclining towards sin. (فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): that is, to him; the pronoun referring back to the mubtadaʾ has been omitted.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَا أُحِلَّ لَهُمْ قُلْ أُحِلَّ لَكُمُ الطَّيِّبَاتُ وَمَا عَلَّمْتُمْ مِنَ الْجَوَارِحِ مُكَلِّبِينَ تُعَلِّمُونَهُنَّ مِمَّا عَلَّمَكُمُ اللَّهُ فَكُلُوا مِمَّا أَمْسَكْنَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَاذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ) (٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَاذَا أُحِلَّ لَهُمْ): it has been mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Baqara.
(وَمَا عَلَّمْتُمْ): «مَا» is in the sense of الذي (relative noun), and the implied form is: "the game of what you have taught", or "the teaching of what you have taught". And (مِنَ الْجَوَارِحِ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted hāʾ, or from ما. الجوارح is the plural of جارحة (hunting animal), and the hāʾ in it is for intensiveness; it is an adjective that has become predominant [as a noun], since the qualified noun is hardly ever mentioned with it. (مُكَلِّبِينَ): it is read with doubling and without doubling. One says كلّبتُ الكلبَ and أكلبتُه, so it became trained (كُلِّب), that is: I incited it against the game; and أسّدتُه, so it became fierce like a lion (استأسد). It is a ḥāl from the pronoun in عُلِّمتم «[Translator's note: so vowelled in the text; the verse has عَلَّمْتُمْ.]». (تُعَلِّمُونَهُنَّ): there are two views on it. The first: it is resumptive, with no grammatical position. The second: it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in مكلّبين. It may not be a second ḥāl, because a single operator does not govern two ḥāls; nor is it good to make it a ḥāl from الجوارح, because you would have separated between them by a ḥāl belonging to something other than الجوارح. (مِمَّا): that is, of what «عَلَّمَكُمُ اللَّهُ».

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الْيَوْمَ أُحِلَّ لَكُمُ الطَّيِّبَاتُ وَطَعَامُ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ حِلٌّ لَكُمْ وَطَعَامُكُمْ حِلٌّ لَهُمْ وَالْمُحْصَنَاتُ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ وَالْمُحْصَنَاتُ مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ إِذَا آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ مُحْصِنِينَ غَيْرَ مُسَافِحِينَ وَلَا مُتَّخِذِي أَخْدَانٍ وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِالْإِيمَانِ فَقَدْ حَبِطَ عَمَلُهُ وَهُوَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ) (٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَطَعَامُ الَّذِينَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «وَحِلٌّ لَكُمْ» is its khabar (predicate). It may also be conjoined to الطيبات, and حلّ لكم is then the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. (وَطَعَامُكُمْ حِلٌّ لَهُمْ): mubtadaʾ and khabar. (وَالْمُحْصَنَاتُ): conjoined to الطيبات; it may also be a mubtadaʾ with the khabar omitted, that is: and chaste women among the believers are lawful for you as well. And (حِلٌّ) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of الحلال (lawful), so it is not put in the dual or plural. And (مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in المحصنات, or from المحصنات itself if you conjoin it to الطيبات. (إِذَا آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ): an adverb (ẓarf) of أُحلّ, or of the omitted «حِلٌّ». (مُحْصِنِينَ):
a ḥāl from the nominative pronoun in آتيتموهن, so the operator is آتيتم; the operator may also be أُحلّ or the omitted «حِلٌّ». (غَيْرَ): an adjective (ṣifa) of محصنين, or a ḥāl from the pronoun that is in it. (وَلَا مُتَّخِذِي): conjoined to «غَيْرَ», so it is accusative (manṣūb); it may also be conjoined to مسافحين, and لا is then for reinforcing the negation. (وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِالْإِيمَانِ): that is, in that which is believed in; so it is a maṣdar in the position of the object, like الخلق in the sense of المخلوق (the created). It has also been said that the implied form is: "in the One who makes faith obligatory", and He is Allah. (وَهُوَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ): its i'rab is like the i'rab of (وَإِنَّهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ لَمِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ), and it has been mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Baqara.

ukberi-tibyan:70-70.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَقَدْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ وَأَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْهِمْ رُسُلًا كُلَّمَا جَاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ بِمَا لَا تَهْوَى أَنْفُسُهُمْ فَرِيقًا كَذَّبُوا وَفَرِيقًا يَقْتُلُونَ) (٧٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَرِيقًا كَذَّبُوا وَفَرِيقًا): the first «فَرِيقًا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of كَذَّبُوا, and the second is the mafʿūl bihi of «يَقْتُلُونَ». And كَذَّبُوا is the answer (jawāb) of كُلَّمَا, and يَقْتُلُونَ has the meaning of قَتَلُوا ("they killed"); it came in this form only so that the verse-endings would agree.

ukberi-tibyan:71-71.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَحَسِبُوا أَلَّا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ فَعَمُوا وَصَمُّوا ثُمَّ تَابَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ ثُمَّ عَمُوا وَصَمُّوا كَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ) (٧١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَلَّا تَكُونَ): it is read with the accusative (naṣb), on the view that «أَنِ» is the one that puts the verb in the accusative, and حَسِبُوا has the meaning of doubt.
And it is read with the nominative (rafʿ), on the view that «أَنِ» is the one lightened from the heavy (أَنَّ), and its khabar (predicate) is omitted. That is permitted because «لَا» has separated it from the verb; and on this view حَسِبُوا has the meaning of عَلِمُوا ("they knew"). Both usages have occurred with it. The lightened أَنْ (from the heavy) may not occur with verbs of doubt and hope, nor the أَنْ that puts the verb in the accusative with عَلِمْتُ and what has its meaning. And كَانَ here is the complete (tāmma) one. (فَعَمُوا وَصَمُّوا): this is the well-known reading.
And it is read with ḍamma on the ʿayn and the ṣād [Translator's note: i.e. عُمُوا وَصُمُّوا], and this belongs to the pattern of زُكِمَ ("he caught a cold") and أَزْكَمَهُ اللَّهُ ("Allah gave him a cold"); one does not say عَمِيتُهُ and صَمَمْتُهُ; rather it came without the hamza only in the passive (what has not had its agent named), and that is rare; the widespread usage is أَعْمَى and أَصَمَّ.
(كَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ): it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "the blindness and deafness are many". It is also said: it is a badal (substitute) for the agent pronoun in صَمُّوا. It is also said: it is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause before it is a khabar of it, i.e. "many of them became blind"; this is weak, because the verb has occurred in its own place, so nothing else is intended by it. It is also said: the wāw is a sign of the plural, not a noun (pronoun), and كَثِيرٌ is the fāʿil (agent) of صَمُّوا.

ukberi-tibyan:73-73.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَقَدْ كَفَرَ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ ثَالِثُ ثَلَاثَةٍ وَمَا مِنْ إِلَهٍ إِلَّا إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ وَإِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهُوا عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ لَيَمَسَّنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ) (٧٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ثَالِثُ ثَلَاثَةٍ): i.e. "one of three"; in an expression like this only the genitive construct (iḍāfa) is permitted. (وَمَا مِنْ إِلَهٍ): مِنْ is redundant (zāʾida), and «إِلَهٍ» is in the position of a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "and creation has no god".
(إِلَّا إِلَهٌ): a badal (substitute) for إِلَهٍ; and had it been read in the genitive as a badal for the wording of إِلَهٍ, that would be permissible in Arabic. (لَيَمَسَّنَّ): the answer of an omitted oath, and it stands in place of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition, which is «وَإِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهُوا». And (مِنْهُمْ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), either from الَّذِينَ or from the agent pronoun in كَفَرُوا.

ukberi-tibyan:75-75.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَا الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ وَأُمُّهُ صِدِّيقَةٌ كَانَا يَأْكُلَانِ الطَّعَامَ انْظُرْ كَيْفَ نُبَيِّنُ لَهُمُ الْآيَاتِ ثُمَّ انْظُرْ أَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ) (٧٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ): in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of رَسُولٍ. (كَانَا يَأْكُلَانِ الطَّعَامَ): it has no grammatical position. (أَنَّى): with the meaning of كَيْفَ ("how"), in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), and what governs it is «يُؤْفَكُونَ». «انْظُرْ» does not govern it, because an interrogative is not governed by what precedes it.

ukberi-tibyan:76-76.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ أَتَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مَا لَا يَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ ضَرًّا وَلَا نَفْعًا وَاللَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ) (٧٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا لَا يَمْلِكُ): مَا may be an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa), and it may have the meaning of الَّذِي ("that which").

ukberi-tibyan:77-77.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ لَا تَغْلُوَا فِي دِينِكُمْ غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا أَهْوَاءَ قَوْمٍ قَدْ ضَلُّوا.) (٧٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تَغْلُوا): an intransitive verb.
And (غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ): a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "an exceeding other than the truth". It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun, i.e. "do not exceed bounds, overstepping the truth".

ukberi-tibyan:78-78.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لُعِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ عَلَى لِسَانِ دَاوُدَ وَعِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ ذَلِكَ بِمَا عَصَوْا وَكَانُوا يَعْتَدُونَ) (٧٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا», or from the agent pronoun in كَفَرُوا. (عَلَى لِسَانِ دَاوُدَ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to «لَعَنَ», as when you say جَاءَ زَيْدٌ عَلَى الْفَرَسِ ("Zayd came on the horse"). [Translator's note: the source writes «لَعَنَ» here, while the verse has the passive لُعِنَ.] (ذَلِكَ بِمَا عَصَوْا): its mention has preceded in more than one place, and likewise (لَبِئْسَ مَا كَانُوا) and «لَبِئْسَ مَا قَدَّمَتْ لَهُمْ».
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ سَخِطَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ) [Translator's note: this is from verse 80]: أَنْ with the verb is in the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the nominative, the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is Allah's displeasure".
It is also said: it is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) for «مَا», i.e. "evil as a thing is that Allah was displeased with them". It is also said: it is in the position of the genitive by an omitted lām, i.e. "because Allah was displeased".

ukberi-tibyan:82-82.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَتَجِدَنَّ أَشَدَّ النَّاسِ عَدَاوَةً لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا الْيَهُودَ وَالَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا وَلَتَجِدَنَّ أَقْرَبَهُمْ مَوَدَّةً لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا الَّذِينَ قَالُوا إِنَّا نَصَارَى ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ مِنْهُمْ قِسِّيسِينَ وَرُهْبَانًا وَأَنَّهُمْ لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ) (٨٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَدَاوَةً): a tamyīz (specification), and what governs it is «أَشَدَّ». And (لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): attached (mutaʿalliq) to the maṣdar (verbal noun), or a naʿt (adjective) of it. (الْيَهُودَ): the second object of «تَجِدَ». (ذَلِكَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (بِأَنَّ مِنْهُمْ) is the khabar (predicate), i.e. "that is existing by this description".

ukberi-tibyan:83-83.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا سَمِعُوا مَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَى الرَّسُولِ تَرَى أَعْيُنَهُمْ تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدَّمْعِ مِمَّا عَرَفُوا مِنَ الْحَقِّ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا آمَنَّا فَاكْتُبْنَا مَعَ الشَّاهِدِينَ) (٨٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِذَا سَمِعُوا): the wāw here has conjoined إِذَا to the khabar (predicate) of أَنَّ, which is His saying «لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ», so the statement has come within the ṣila of أَنَّ. إِذَا is in the position of the accusative governed by «تَرَى», and إِذَا with its answer is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the khabar of the second أَنَّ. It may also be resumptive in wording, even though it has a connection with what precedes it in meaning. And (تَفِيضُ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because تَرَى is from seeing with the eye. And (مِنَ الدَّمْعِ): there are two views on it. First: that مِنْ marks the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), i.e. their overflowing is from the abundance of tears. Second: that it is a ḥāl; the implied wording is "overflowing, filled with tears". As for (مِمَّا عَرَفُوا): مِنْ marks the beginning of the extent, and its meaning is "because of what they recognised". And (مِنَ الْحَقِّ): a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun (ʿāʾid). (يَقُولُونَ): a ḥāl from the agent pronoun in عَرَفُوا.

ukberi-tibyan:84-84.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا لَنَا لَا نُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَمَا جَاءَنَا مِنَ الْحَقِّ وَنَطْمَعُ أَنْ يُدْخِلَنَا رَبُّنَا مَعَ الْقَوْمِ الصَّالِحِينَ) (٨٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا لَنَا): «مَا» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and لَنَا is the khabar (predicate). And (لَا نُؤْمِنُ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the khabar, and what governs it is the preposition, i.e. "what is with us, not believing?", as you say مَا لَكَ قَائِمًا ("why are you standing?"). (وَمَا جَاءَنَا): it may be in the position of the genitive, i.e. "and in what has come to us". (مِنَ الْحَقِّ): a ḥāl from the agent pronoun; and it may mark the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), i.e. "and in what has come to us from Allah". And it [Translator's note: i.e. مَا] may be a mubtadaʾ, with مِنَ الْحَقِّ as the khabar, and the clause in the position of a ḥāl. (وَنَطْمَعُ): it may be conjoined to نُؤْمِنُ, i.e. "and why should we not hope"; and the implied wording may be "while we hope", so the clause is a ḥāl from the agent pronoun in نُؤْمِنُ. And (أَنْ يُدْخِلَنَا): i.e. "in that He should admit us", so it is in the position of the accusative or the genitive, according to the disagreement between al-Khalīl and Sībawayh.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا قُمْتُمْ إِلَى الصَّلَاةِ فَاغْسِلُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ إِلَى الْمَرَافِقِ وَامْسَحُوا بِرُءُوسِكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ إِلَى الْكَعْبَيْنِ وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ جُنُبًا فَاطَّهَّرُوا وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ مَرْضَى أَوْ عَلَى سَفَرٍ أَوْ جَاءَ أَحَدٌ مِنْكُمْ مِنَ الْغَائِطِ أَوْ لَامَسْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ فَلَمْ تَجِدُوا مَاءً فَتَيَمَّمُوا صَعِيدًا طَيِّبًا فَامْسَحُوا بِوُجُوهِكُمْ وَأَيْدِيكُمْ مِنْهُ مَا يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيَجْعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ حَرَجٍ وَلَكِنْ يُرِيدُ لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ وَلِيُتِمَّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ) (٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَى الْمَرَافِقِ): it has been said that «إِلَى» is in the sense of «مَعَ» ("with"), as in His saying: وَيَزِدْكُمْ قُوَّةً إِلَى قُوَّتِكُمْ. This is not the preferred view; the correct view is that it is in its proper sense and that it marks the end of the extent (intihāʾ al-ghāya). Washing the elbows became obligatory only through the Sunna, and there is no contradiction between them, because «إِلَى» indicates the end of the action and does not address either the exclusion or the inclusion of the limit itself. Do you not see that if you say "I travelled to Kufa" (سرت إلى الكوفة), it is not impossible that you reached its first boundaries without entering it, nor that you entered it? If evidence were established that you entered it, that would not contradict your saying "I travelled to Kufa". On this view «إِلَى» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «اغْسِلُوا».
It may also be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), attached to something omitted, the implied form being: "and your hands, joined to the elbows".
(بِرُءُوسِكُمْ): the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida). Someone with no expertise in Arabic said that the bāʾ in such cases is partitive (li-l-tabʿīḍ), but this is nothing that the grammarians recognise. The reason for its entering is that it indicates the adhering of the wiping to the head. (وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ): it is read in the accusative (naṣb), and there are two views on it.
The first: it is conjoined to الوجوه and الأيدي, that is: "so wash your faces and your hands and your feet". That is permissible in Arabic without disagreement, and the Sunna indicating the obligation of washing the feet strengthens it. The second: that it is conjoined to the position of برءوسكم. The first is stronger, because conjunction on the wording is stronger than conjunction on the position.
In an irregular (shādhdh) reading it is read in the nominative (rafʿ), as a mubtadaʾ (subject), that is: "and your feet are to be washed likewise". It is also read in the genitive (jarr), and this is well known too, as well known as the accusative, and there are two views on it. The first: that it is conjoined to الرءوس in i'rab, while the ruling differs: the heads are wiped and the feet are washed. This is the i'rab that is said to be by contiguity (jiwār), and it is not impossible for it to occur in the Qur'an because of how common it is; it has indeed come in the Qur'an and in poetry. From the Qur'an there is His saying, Exalted is He: (وَحُورٌ عِينٌ) on the reading of those who put it in the genitive, it being conjoined to His saying (بِأَكْوَابٍ وَأَبَارِيقَ) while the meaning differs, since the meaning is not "immortal youths will circulate among them with wide-eyed houris". The poet — al-Nābigha — said:
لَمْ يَبْقَ إِلَّا أَسِيرٌ غَيْرُ مُنْفَلِتٍ أَوْ مُوثَقٍ فِي حِبَالِ الْقَيْدِ مَجْنُوبُ
(None remained but a captive unable to escape, or one bound in the ropes of the fetter, led along.)
— and the rhymes are in the genitive «[Translator's note: i.e. موثقٍ is genitive by contiguity with منفلتٍ although it is conjoined to the nominative أسير.]». Contiguity is well known among them in i'rab, in the changing of letters into one another, in the feminine, and in other things. From i'rab is what we have mentioned regarding conjunction; and from adjectives there is His saying: (عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ مُحِيطٍ), while the day is not encompassing — it is only the punishment that encompasses.
Likewise His saying: (فِي يَوْمٍ عَاصِفٍ), while the day is not stormy — it is only the wind that is stormy. From the changing of letters there is his saying, upon him be blessing and peace: «ارْجِعْنَ مَأْزُورَاتٍ غَيْرَ مَأْجُورَاتٍ» ("Go back burdened with sin, not rewarded"); the original is موزورات, but correspondence [with مأجورات] was intended. Likewise their saying: إنه لا يأتينا بالغدايا والعشايا ("he does not come to us in the mornings and the evenings"). From the feminine there is His saying: (فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا), where the tāʾ has been dropped from عشر although it is annexed to الأمثال, which is masculine; but since الأمثال is contiguous with the feminine pronoun, its rule was applied to it. Likewise the saying of the poet:
لَمَّا أَتَى خَبَرُ الزُّبَيْرِ تَضَعْضَعَتْ ... سُورُ الْمَدِينَةِ وَالْجِبَالُ الْخُشَّعُ
(When the news of al-Zubayr came, the wall of the city was shaken, and the humbled mountains.)
and their saying: ذهبت بعض أصابعه ("some of his fingers went").
Among the things in which the Arabs observed contiguity is their saying قامت هند ("Hind stood"): they did not allow dropping the tāʾ when nothing separates the two, but if they separated them they allowed dropping it, and there is no difference between the two cases except contiguity and the absence of
contiguity. Of that kind also is their saying قام زيد وعمرًا كلمته ("Zayd stood, and ʿAmr I spoke to him"): they considered the accusative, by an omitted verb, to be good because the clause is contiguous with a noun that a verb has governed. Of that kind also is their changing of the wāw that is next to the end of the word into hamza in their word أوائل, just as if it had occurred at the end; and likewise, when it is far from the end it is not changed, as in طواويس. This is a topic on which pages of evidence could be written; the grammarians have devoted a chapter to it and built questions upon it, and then they established it as a principle on the basis of their saying «جُحْرُ ضَبٍّ خَرِبٍ» ("a ruined lizard's hole"), to the point that they disagreed about whether the genitive [by contiguity] is permissible in the dual and the plural. A group of the most skilful of them allowed the following [in case] (itbāʿ) in both, by analogy with the attested singular; and if it had no basis in analogy at all, they would have restricted it to what is attested only. What supports what we have mentioned is that, besides the genitive in the verse, other [readings] have been allowed, namely the accusative and the nominative, and the nominative and accusative are neither decisive nor apparent in [indicating] that the ruling for the feet is wiping; so likewise the genitive must be like the accusative and the nominative in ruling, though not in i'rab. The second view: that the genitive of الأرجل is by an omitted preposition, its implied form being: "and do washing to your feet" (وافعلوا بأرجلكم غسلًا). Omitting the preposition while keeping the genitive is permissible; the poet said:
مَشَائِيمُ لَيْسُوا مُصْلِحِينَ عَشِيرَةً ... وَلَا نَاعِبٍ إِلَّا بِبَيْنٍ غُرَابُهَا
(Ill-omened men, not ones who set a clan aright, nor is their raven one that croaks except of separation.)
And Zuhayr said:
بَدَا لِيَ أَنِّي لَسْتُ مُدْرِكَ مَا مَضَى ... وَلَا سَابِقٍ شَيْئًا إِذَا كَانَ جَائِيًا
(It has become clear to me that I cannot overtake what has passed, nor outstrip anything when it is coming.)
So it was put in the genitive by implying the bāʾ, and it is not a place of poetic necessity. I have devoted a separate book to this question.
(إِلَى الْكَعْبَيْنِ): like «إِلَى الْمَرَافِقِ». In it there is evidence for the obligation of washing the feet, because what is wiped is not given a limit; the limiting is in what is washed when part of it is meant, which is His saying: «وَأَيْدِيكُمْ إِلَى الْمَرَافِقِ», and He did not limit the face because the whole of it is meant. (وَأَيْدِيكُمْ مِنْهُ): «مِنْهُ» is in the position of the accusative by امسحوا. (لِيَجْعَلَ): the lām is not redundant, and the object of يريد is omitted, its implied form being: "Allah does not want the concession of tayammum in order to place hardship upon you". It has also been said that the lām is redundant, but this is weak, because أن is not pronounced, and the verb can only properly be the object of «يُرِيدُ» with أن. Similar to it is (وَلَكِنْ يُرِيدُ لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ), that is: He wants that in order to purify you. (عَلَيْكُمْ): attached to يُتمّ; it may also be attached to النعمة, and it may be a ḥāl from النعمة.

ukberi-tibyan:88-88.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكُلُوا مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ حَلَالًا طَيِّبًا وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي أَنْتُمْ بِهِ مُؤْمِنُونَ) (٨٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حَلَالًا): there are three views on it. First: it is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of كُلُوا; on this view «مِمَّا» is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it is a naʿt (adjective) of the indefinite noun placed before it. And «مِنْ» may mark the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya) of eating, so it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to كُلُوا, as when you say أَكَلْتُ مِنَ الْخُبْزِ رَغِيفًا ("I ate a loaf of the bread"), if the adjectival sense is not intended. The second view: that it is a ḥāl from «مَا», because it has the meaning of الَّذِي; and it may be a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun (ʿāʾid), in which case what governs it is «رَزَقَ». The third: that it is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a lawful eating". حَلَالًا may not be put in the accusative by رَزَقَ as its object, because that would prevent a pronoun from returning to «مَا».

ukberi-tibyan:89-89.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَا يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ اللَّهُ بِاللَّغْوِ فِي أَيْمَانِكُمْ وَلَكِنْ يُؤَاخِذُكُمْ بِمَا عَقَّدْتُمُ الْأَيْمَانَ فَكَفَّارَتُهُ إِطْعَامُ عَشَرَةِ مَسَاكِينَ مِنْ أَوْسَطِ مَا تُطْعِمُونَ أَهْلِيكُمْ أَوْ كِسْوَتُهُمْ أَوْ تَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ ذَلِكَ كَفَّارَةُ أَيْمَانِكُمْ إِذَا حَلَفْتُمْ وَاحْفَظُوا أَيْمَانَكُمْ كَذَلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ آيَاتِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ) (٨٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِاللَّغْوِ فِي أَيْمَانِكُمْ): there are three views on it. First: that it [Translator's note: i.e. فِي] is attached (mutaʿalliq) to اللَّغْوِ itself, because you say لَغَا فِي يَمِينِهِ ("he spoke idly in his oath"); this is a maṣdar (verbal noun) with alif and lām that governs, but it is made transitive by a preposition. Second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from اللَّغْوِ, i.e. "for idle speech being, or occurring, in your oaths". Third: that «فِي» is attached to «يُؤَاخِذُكُمْ». (عَقَّدْتُمُ): it is read with the qāf unshadded, and that is the original; "binding the oath" is intending commitment to it. And it is read with it shadded, and that is for emphasising the oath, as in His saying «هُوَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ» and the like. It is also said: the shadda indicates the emphasis of resolve in committing to it. It is also said: it was shadded only because of the many who swear and the many oaths. It is also said: the shadda is a compensation for the alif in عَاقَدَ. The shadda may not be for repetition of the oath, because the expiation is obligatory even if it is not repeated.
And it is read «عَاقَدْتُمْ» with alif, and it has the meaning of عَقَدْتُمْ, as when you say قَاطَعْتُهُ and قَطَعْتُهُ ("I cut him off") in the sense of shunning.
(فَكَفَّارَتُهُ): the hāʾ is the pronoun of the binding (al-ʿaqd), the verb indicating it having preceded. It is also said: it refers back to the oath by meaning, because the swearing and the oath have one meaning. And (إِطْعَامُ): a maṣdar in genitive construct with the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the best is that it be taken as implying a verb whose agent is named (active), because what precedes it and what follows it is address; so on this view «عَشَرَةَ» is in the position of the accusative.
(مِنْ أَوْسَطِ): a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted object, its implied form being "if you feed ten poor persons food, or sustenance, from the average", i.e. "middling". (مَا تُطْعِمُونَ): i.e. "that from which you feed", or "which you feed them". (أَوْ كِسْوَتُهُمْ): conjoined to «إِطْعَامُ»; and it is read in an irregular (shādhdh) reading as (أَوْ كَإِسْوَتِهِمْ), in which case the kāf is in the position of the nominative, i.e. "or the like of the example of your families in clothing". (أَوْ تَحْرِيرُ): conjoined to «إِطْعَامُ», and it too is a maṣdar in genitive construct with the object. (إِذَا حَلَفْتُمْ): what governs إِذَا is «كَفَّارَةُ أَيْمَانِكُمْ», because the meaning is "that expiates your oaths at the time of your swearing". (كَذَلِكَ): the kāf is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "He makes clear to you His signs with a making-clear like that".

ukberi-tibyan:90-90.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّمَا الْخَمْرُ وَالْمَيْسِرُ وَالْأَنْصَابُ وَالْأَزْلَامُ رِجْسٌ مِنْ عَمَلِ الشَّيْطَانِ فَاجْتَنِبُوهُ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ) (٩٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (رِجْسٌ): it was made singular only because the implied wording is "the practice of these things is only filth". It may also be a khabar (predicate) of الْخَمْرُ, with the predicates of the conjoined nouns omitted because the predicate of the first indicates them. And (مِنْ عَمَلِ): a naʿt (adjective) of رِجْسٍ, or a second khabar. The hāʾ in (اجْتَنِبُوهُ) refers back to the practice, or to the filth; and the implied wording is "filth of the kind of Satan's work".

ukberi-tibyan:91-91.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ الشَّيْطَانُ أَنْ يُوقِعَ بَيْنَكُمُ الْعَدَاوَةَ وَالْبَغْضَاءَ فِي الْخَمْرِ وَالْمَيْسِرِ وَيَصُدَّكُمْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَعَنِ الصَّلَاةِ فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُنْتَهُونَ) (٩١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي الْخَمْرِ وَالْمَيْسِرِ): «فِي» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يُوقِعَ», and it has the meaning of cause, i.e. "because of drinking wine and practising gambling".
And فِي may be attached to الْعَدَاوَةَ or to الْبَغْضَاءَ, i.e. "that you become enemies and hate one another because of drinking"; on this view it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) with alif and lām that is made to govern. The hamza in الْبَغْضَاءَ is for the feminine, and it is not the feminine of the afʿal pattern, since the masculine of الْبَغْضَاءُ is not أَبْغَضُ; it is like الْبَأْسَاءُ and الضَّرَّاءُ. (فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُنْتَهُونَ): its wording is interrogative and its meaning is command, i.e. "desist!"; but the interrogative immediately after the mention of these vices is more eloquent than the command.

ukberi-tibyan:93-93.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَيْسَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ جنَاح فِيمَا طعموا إِذا مَا اتَّقوا وآمنوا وَعمِلُوا الصَّالِحَات) (٩٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذَا مَا اتَّقَوْا): what governs إِذَا is the meaning of "there is no blame on those who believe and do righteous deeds", i.e. "they do not sin when they are mindful (of Allah)".

ukberi-tibyan:94-94.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَيَبْلُوَنَّكُمُ اللَّهُ بِشَيْءٍ مِنَ الصَّيْدِ تَنَالُهُ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَرِمَاحُكُمْ لِيَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَخَافُهُ بِالْغَيْبِ فَمَنِ اعْتَدَى بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَلَهُ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ) (٩٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنَ الصَّيْدِ): in the position of the genitive, a naʿt (adjective) of شَيْءٍ, and «مِنَ» is for clarifying the genus. It is also said: it is partitive, since game is forbidden only in the state of iḥrām, in the sacred precinct, and on land. الصَّيْدُ is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), and here it has the meaning of الْمَصِيدُ ("what is hunted"); it was called مَصِيدٌ and صَيْدٌ because of what it comes to, and because the motives for hunting it are abundant; so it is as though, when it was made ready for hunting, it became as if hunted. (تَنَالُهُ): a naʿt of شَيْءٍ. It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from شَيْءٍ, because it has been qualified, or a ḥāl from الصَّيْدِ.
(لِيَعْلَمَ): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «لِيَبْلُونَّكُمْ». (بِالْغَيْبِ): it may be in the position of a ḥāl from «مَنْ» or from the agent pronoun in يَخَافُهُ, i.e. "fears Him while hidden from people"; and it may have the meaning of «فِي», i.e. "in the place hidden from people". الْغَيْبُ is a maṣdar in place of an active participle (fāʿil).

ukberi-tibyan:95-95.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَقْتُلُوا الصَّيْدَ وَأَنْتُمْ حُرُمٌ وَمَنْ قَتَلَهُ مِنْكُمْ مُتَعَمِّدًا فَجَزَاءٌ مِثْلُ مَا قَتَلَ مِنَ النَّعَمِ يَحْكُمُ بِهِ ذَوَا عَدْلٍ مِنْكُمْ هَدْيًا بَالِغَ الْكَعْبَةِ أَوْ كَفَّارَةٌ طَعَامُ مَسَاكِينَ أَوْ عَدْلُ ذَلِكَ صِيَامًا لِيَذُوقَ وَبَالَ أَمْرِهِ عَفَا اللَّهُ عَمَّا سَلَفَ وَمَنْ عَادَ فَيَنْتَقِمُ اللَّهُ مِنْهُ وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ ذُو انْتِقَامٍ) (٩٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَنْتُمْ حُرُمٌ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in تَقْتُلُوا. And (مُتَعَمِّدًا): a ḥāl from the agent pronoun in قَتَلَهُ. (فَجَزَاءٌ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted; it is also said that the implied wording is "then what is due is a recompense".
And it is read with tanwīn (nunation); on this view «مِثْلُ» is a naʿt (adjective) of it or a badal (substitute), and مِثْلُ here has the meaning of مُمَاثِلٌ ("equivalent"). On this reading مِنَ النَّعَمِ may not be attached to «جَزَاءٌ», because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and what is attached to it is part of its ṣila, and separating the ṣila from what it is linked to (the mawṣūl) by a naʿt or a badal is not permitted, because the mawṣūl is not yet complete, so it is not qualified nor substituted for.
And it is read in an irregular (shādhdh) reading as «جَزَاءً» with tanwīn, and مِثْلَ in the accusative, its accusative being by «جَزَاءً». It may also be in the accusative by a verb indicated by «جَزَاءٌ», i.e. "he brings out" or "he pays the like"; and this is preferable, because جَزَاءٌ is made transitive by a preposition.
And in the well-known reading it is read with جَزَاءُ in genitive construct with مِثْلِ; the i'rab of جَزَاءُ is as given above, and «مِثْلُ» in this reading has the status of something redundant, as in their saying مِثْلِي لَا يَقُولُ ذَلِكَ ("the like of me does not say that"), i.e. "I do not say it". What called for this interpretation is that what makes the recompense due is the animal killed, not its like.
As for (مِنَ النَّعَمِ): there are several views on it. First: that you make it a ḥāl from the pronoun in قَتَلَ, because the animal killed is of livestock. Second: that it is a naʿt of جَزَاءٌ when you give it tanwīn, i.e. "a recompense being from livestock". Third: that you attach it to جَزَاءُ itself when you put it in genitive construct, because the muḍāf ilayhi is included in the muḍāf, so it does not count as a separation between the ṣila and the mawṣūl.
And likewise if you give جَزَاءً tanwīn and put «مِثْلًا» in the accusative, because it governs both of them, so they are both part of its ṣila, as you say يُعْجِبُنِي ضَرْبُكَ زَيْدًا بِالسَّوْطِ ("your beating Zayd with the whip pleases me").
(يَحْكُمُ بِهِ): in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of جَزَاءٌ when I give it tanwīn; as for the genitive-construct reading, it is in the position of a ḥāl, and what governs it is the meaning of settledness (al-istiqrār) implied in the omitted khabar. (ذَوَا عَدْلٍ): the alif is for the dual; and it is read in an irregular reading as «ذُو» in the singular, meaning the genus, just as «مِنْ» is construed according to the meaning; so on this view its implied form is "a party possessing justice" or "a judge possessing justice". And (مِنْكُمْ): a naʿt of ذَوَا; it may not be a naʿt of الْعَدْلِ, because عَدْلٌ here is a maṣdar, not an adjective. (هَدْيًا): a ḥāl from the hāʾ in بِهِ, with the meaning of مَهْدِيٌّ ("offered as a sacrifice"); it is also said: it is a maṣdar, i.e. "he offers it as an offering"; and it is also said: it is a tamyīz (specification). And (بَالِغَ الْكَعْبَةِ): a naʿt of هَدْيًا, with the tanwīn implied, i.e. بَالِغًا الْكَعْبَةَ. (أَوْ كَفَّارَةٌ): conjoined to جَزَاءٌ, i.e. "or upon him is an expiation", if the like is not found. And (طَعَامُ): a badal for كَفَّارَةٌ, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is the feeding". And it is read with the genitive construct [Translator's note: i.e. كَفَّارَةُ طَعَامِ], and the genitive construct here is for clarifying the muḍāf. And (صِيَامًا): a tamyīz.
(لِيَذُوقَ): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the settledness, i.e. "the recompense is upon him so that he may taste"; and it may be attached to صِيَامًا, or to طَعَامُ. (فَيَنْتَقِمُ اللَّهُ): the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and this is good because the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) is past in wording.

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَمِيثَاقَهُ الَّذِي وَاثَقَكُمْ بِهِ إِذْ قُلْتُمْ سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ) (٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ): an adverb (ẓarf) of واثقكم; it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the genitive hāʾ, or a ḥāl from الميثاق.
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ لِلَّهِ شُهَدَاءَ بِالْقِسْطِ وَلَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَآنُ قَوْمٍ عَلَى أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا اعْدِلُوا هُوَ أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَى وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ) (٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (شُهَدَاءَ بِالْقِسْطِ): like His saying, Exalted is He: {شُهَدَاء لله}, and we have mentioned it in [Sūrat] al-Nisāʾ.
(هُوَ أَقْرَبُ): هو is the pronoun of justice (العدل), and اعدلوا has indicated it. أقرب للتقوى has been mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Baqara.

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَأَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ) (٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَعَدَ اللَّهُ): وعد is transitive to two objects, and it is permissible to confine it to one of them. The first object here is «الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا», and the second is omitted, dispensed with by the clause that is His saying «لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ», which has no grammatical position, because وعد is not suspended from governing (taʿlīq) as ظننت and its sisters are suspended.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ هَمَّ قَوْمٌ أَنْ يَبْسُطُوا إِلَيْكُمْ أَيْدِيَهُمْ فَكَفَّ أَيْدِيَهُمْ عَنْكُمْ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ) (١١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ): [عليكم] is attached (mutaʿalliq) to نعمة; it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it, and then it is attached to something omitted. And (إِذْ) is also an adverb (ẓarf) of النعمة; if you make عليكم a ḥāl, it may govern إذ. (أَنْ يَبْسُطُوا): that is, بأن يبسطوا ("to stretch out"), and we have mentioned the disagreement about its position.

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَقَدْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثَاقَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ وَبَعَثْنَا مِنْهُمُ اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ نَقِيبًا وَقَالَ اللَّهُ إِنِّي مَعَكُمْ لَئِنْ أَقَمْتُمُ الصَّلَاةَ وَآتَيْتُمُ الزَّكَاةَ وَآمَنْتُمْ بِرُسُلِي وَعَزَّرْتُمُوهُمْ وَأَقْرَضْتُمُ اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا لَأُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ وَلَأُدْخِلَنَّكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ فَمَنْ كَفَرَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ مِنْكُمْ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ) (١٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْهُمُ اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ): منهم may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to بعثنا, or it may be an adjective (ṣifa) of اثني عشر that has been placed first and so has become a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَعَزَّرْتُمُوهُمْ): it is read with doubling and without doubling, and the meaning is the same. (قَرْضًا): it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun) with its augment letters dropped, governed by أقرضتم, that is: إقراضًا ("lending"); and القرض may be in the sense of المُقرَض (the thing lent), so that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (لَأُكَفِّرَنَّ): the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (فَمَنْ كَفَرَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ مِنْكُمْ): in the position of a ḥāl from the pronoun in لأكفرنّ «[Translator's note: so in the text; the remark evidently concerns منكم.]». And (سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ) has been mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Baqara.

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ مِيثَاقَهُمْ لَعَنَّاهُمْ وَجَعَلْنَا قُلُوبَهُمْ قَاسِيَةً يُحَرِّفُونَ الْكَلِمَ عَنْ مَوَاضِعِهِ وَنَسُوا حَظًّا مِمَّا ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ وَلَا تَزَالُ تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى خَائِنَةٍ مِنْهُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِنْهُمْ فَاعْفُ عَنْهُمْ وَاصْفَحْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ) (١٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ): the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «لَعَنَّاهُمْ»; had the verb come first, the fāʾ would have entered on it. ما is redundant (zāʾida), or in the sense of "a thing", and it has been mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Nisāʾ. (وَجَعَلْنَا): transitive to two objects, in the sense of "We made". And (قَاسِيَةً) is the second object; its yāʾ is originally a wāw, because it is from القسوة (hardness).
It is also read «قَسِيَّةً», on the pattern فعيلة: the wāw was changed into yāʾ and the yāʾ of فعيل was assimilated into it, and فعيلة here is for intensiveness, in the sense of فاعلة. (يُحَرِّفُونَ): resumptive; it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object in لعنّاهم, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in قاسية. It may not be a ḥāl from القلوب, because the pronoun in يحرّفون does not refer to القلوب; and it is weak to make it a ḥāl from the hāʾ and mīm in «قُلُوبِهِمْ». (عَنْ مَوَاضِعِهِ): it has been mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Nisāʾ. (عَلَى خَائِنَةٍ): that is, upon a treacherous party; and the pattern فاعلة here may be a maṣdar (verbal noun), like العاقبة and العافية. And (مِنْهُمْ) is an adjective (ṣifa) of خائنة. It is also read «خِيَانَةٍ», which is a maṣdar, and the yāʾ is changed from a wāw, because of their saying يخون, and "so-and-so is more treacherous (أخون) than so-and-so", and "he is خوّان (very treacherous)". (إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِنْهُمْ): an exception from خائنة; if it had been read in the genitive as a badal (substitute), it would have been sound.

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا إِنَّا نَصَارَى أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَهُمْ فَنَسُوا حَظًّا مِمَّا ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ فَأَغْرَيْنَا بَيْنَهُمُ الْعَدَاوَةَ وَالْبَغْضَاءَ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ وَسَوْفَ يُنَبِّئُهُمُ اللَّهُ بِمَا كَانُوا يَصْنَعُونَ) (١٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا): «مِنْ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أخذنا, its implied form being: "and We took from those who said 'We are Christians' their covenant". The speech is conjoined to His saying: (وَلَقَدْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثَاقَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ), and the implied form is: "and We took from those who said 'We are Christians' their covenant".
The implied form may not be: "and We took their covenant from those who said 'We are Christians'", because that involves a pronoun before its referent is mentioned, both in wording and in implied order. The yāʾ in (فأَغْرَيْنَا) is from a wāw, and its derivation is from الغِراء (glue), which is that with which something is stuck; one says سهم مغروّ ("a glued arrow"). And (بَيْنَهُمْ) is an adverb (ẓarf) of أغرينا, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الْعَدَاوَةِ»; it cannot be an adverb of العداوة, because the maṣdar (verbal noun) does not govern what comes before it. (إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ): attached to أغرينا, or to البغضاء, or to العداوة, that is: they hated one another until the Day of Resurrection.

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ قَدْ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولُنَا يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ كَثِيرًا مِمَّا كُنْتُمْ تُخْفُونَ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ وَيَعْفُو عَنْ كَثِيرٍ قَدْ جَاءَكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ نُورٌ وَكِتَابٌ مُبِينٌ) (١٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «رَسُولُنَا». And (مِنَ الْكِتَابِ) is a ḥāl from the omitted hāʾ in تخفون. (قَدْ جَاءَكُمْ): it has no grammatical position. (مِنَ اللَّهِ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to جاءكم, or a ḥāl from «نُورٌ».

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَهْدِي بِهِ اللَّهُ مَنِ اتَّبَعَ رِضْوَانَهُ سُبُلَ السَّلَامِ وَيُخْرِجُهُمْ مِنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى النُّورِ بِإِذْنِهِ وَيَهْدِيهِمْ إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ) (١٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَهْدِي بِهِ اللَّهُ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «رَسُولُنَا», as a badal (substitute) from «يُبَيِّنُ», or a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يُبَيِّنُ»; and it may be an adjective (ṣifa) of «نُورٌ» or of «كِتَابٌ». The hāʾ in به refers to whichever one makes «يَهْدِي» a ḥāl from or an adjective of, and for that reason it is singular. And (مَنْ) is in the sense of الذي (relative noun), or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective. And (سُبُلَ السَّلَامِ) is the second object of «يَهْدِي»; it may also be a badal from رضوانه. الرضوان with kasra and with ḍamma on the rāʾ are two dialectal forms, and it has been read with both. And «سُبُلَ» is with ḍamma on the bāʾ; the sukūn is a dialectal form, and it has been read so. (بِإِذْنِهِ): that is, by means of His command sent down upon His Messenger.

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لَقَدْ كَفَرَ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ قُلْ فَمَنْ يَمْلِكُ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا إِنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يُهْلِكَ الْمَسِيحَ ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ وَأُمَّهُ وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَاءُ وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) (١٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَمَنْ يَمْلِكُ): that is, say to them; and «مَنِ» is an interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīr). And (مِنَ اللَّهِ) may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) attached (mutaʿalliq) to يملك «[Translator's note: so in the text; perhaps "attached to يملك, or a ḥāl" is meant.]», or a ḥāl from شيء. And (جَمِيعًا) is a ḥāl from المسيح, his mother, and those on earth; it may also be a ḥāl from مَن alone. «مَنْ» here is a general term preceded by a particular term of its own kind, namely the Messiah and his mother. (يَخْلُقُ): resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقَالَتِ الْيَهُودُ وَالنَّصَارَى نَحْنُ أَبْنَاءُ اللَّهِ وَأَحِبَّاؤُهُ قُلْ فَلِمَ يُعَذِّبُكُمْ بِذُنُوبِكُمْ بَلْ أَنْتُمْ بَشَرٌ مِمَّنْ خَلَقَ يَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَإِلَيْهِ الْمَصِيرُ) (١٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قُلْ فَلِمَ يُعَذِّبُكُمْ): that is, say to them. (بَلْ أَنْتُمْ): a rejection of their saying «نَحْنُ أَبْنَاءُ اللَّهِ», and it is reported speech governed by قل.

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ قَدْ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولُنَا يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ عَلَى فَتْرَةٍ مِنَ الرُّسُلِ أَنْ تَقُولُوا مَا جَاءَنَا مِنْ بَشِيرٍ وَلَا نَذِيرٍ فَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ بَشِيرٌ وَنَذِيرٌ وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) (١٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَلَى فَتْرَةٍ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in يبيّن; it may also be a ḥāl from the genitive pronoun in لكم. And (مِنَ الرُّسُلِ) is a naʿt (adjective) of فترة. (أَنْ تَقُولُوا): that is, for fear that you should say. (وَلَا نَذِيرٍ): conjoined to the wording of بشير; in [ordinary] speech the nominative would be permissible, [conjoined] to the position of مِن بشير.

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَى لِقَوْمِهِ يَا قَوْمِ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ جَعَلَ فِيكُمْ أَنْبِيَاءَ وَجَعَلَكُمْ مُلُوكًا وَآتَاكُمْ مَا لَمْ يُؤْتِ أَحَدًا مِنَ الْعَالَمِينَ) (٢٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ جَعَلَ): this is like His saying (نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ هَمَّ قَوْمٌ), and it has been mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:21-21.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا قَوْمِ ادْخُلُوا الْأَرْضَ الْمُقَدَّسَةَ الَّتِي كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَلَا تَرْتَدُّوا عَلَى أَدْبَارِكُمْ فَتَنْقَلِبُوا خَاسِرِينَ) (٢١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَلَى أَدْبَارِكُمْ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) in ترتدوا. (فَتَنْقَلِبُوا): it may be jussive (majzūm), conjoined to ترتدوا, or accusative (manṣūb) as the answer to the prohibition.

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا يَا مُوسَى إِنَّ فِيهَا قَوْمًا جَبَّارِينَ وَإِنَّا لَنْ نَدْخُلَهَا حَتَّى يَخْرُجُوا مِنْهَا فَإِنْ يَخْرُجُوا مِنْهَا فَإِنَّا دَاخِلُونَ) (٢٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَإِنَّا دَاخِلُونَ): that is, entering it (داخلوها); the object has been omitted because the speech indicates it.

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ رَجُلَانِ مِنَ الَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمَا ادْخُلُوا عَلَيْهِمُ الْبَابَ فَإِذَا دَخَلْتُمُوهُ فَإِنَّكُمْ غَالِبُونَ وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَتَوَكَّلُوا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ) (٢٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنَ الَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ): in the position of the nominative (rafʿ) as an adjective (ṣifa) of رجلان; يخافون is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, and the wāw is the referring pronoun. It is also read with ḍamma on the yāʾ, as a passive, and it then has two meanings. The first: it is from your saying خِيفَ الرجلُ, that is, "the man was made to fear". The second: that the meaning is "others fear them", as in your saying فلان مخوف, that is, "people fear him". (أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ): another adjective of رجلان; it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), with قد implied with it, and the owner of the ḥāl is رجلان or the pronoun in الذين.

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا يَا مُوسَى إِنَّا لَنْ نَدْخُلَهَا أَبَدًا مَا دَامُوا فِيهَا فَاذْهَبْ أَنْتَ وَرَبُّكَ فَقَاتِلَا إِنَّا هَاهُنَا قَاعِدُونَ) (٢٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا دَامُوا): it is a badal (substitute) from أبدًا, because ما is maṣdariyya and stands in for time, and it is a badal of part [for whole]. And (هَاهُنَا) is an adverb (ẓarf) of «قَاعِدُونَ»; the noun is «هُنَا», and ها is for drawing attention, like that in your saying هذا and هؤلاء.

ukberi-tibyan:25-25.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي لَا أَمْلِكُ إِلَّا نَفْسِي وَأَخِي فَافْرُقْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ الْقَوْمِ الْفَاسِقِينَ) (٢٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَخِي): there are two views on its position. The first: accusative (naṣb), conjoined to نفسي or to the noun of إنّ. The second: nominative (rafʿ), conjoined to the pronoun in أملك, that is: "and my brother possesses only himself". It may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject) with its khabar (predicate) omitted, that is: "and my brother likewise". (وَبَيْنَ الْقَوْمِ الْفَاسِقِينَ): the basic rule is that بين is not repeated, but it may be repeated for emphasis, as in your saying "the property is between Zayd and between ʿAmr"; it has been repeated here so that [القوم] is not conjoined to the pronoun without repeating the preposition.

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ فَإِنَّهَا مُحَرَّمَةٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً يَتِيهُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَلَا تَأْسَ عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْفَاسِقِينَ) (٢٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً): an adverb (ẓarf) of محرّمة, so on this view the prohibition has a fixed term. And (يَتِيهُونَ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the genitive pronoun. It has also been said that it is an adverb of «يَتِيهُونَ», so on this view the prohibition is not limited in time. (فَلَا تَأْسَ): the alif of تأسى is a substitute for a wāw, because it is from الأسى, which is grief, and its dual is أسوان; there is no evidence [to the contrary] in أسيتُ عليه, because of the kasra on the sīn. One also says رجل أسوان ("a grieving man"), with a wāw. It has also been said that it is from yāʾ; one says رجل أسيان as well.

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ ابْنَيْ آدَمَ بِالْحَقِّ إِذْ قَرَّبَا قُرْبَانًا فَتُقُبِّلَ مِنْ أَحَدِهِمَا وَلَمْ يُتَقَبَّلْ مِنَ الْآخَرِ قَالَ لَأَقْتُلَنَّكَ قَالَ إِنَّمَا يَتَقَبَّلُ اللَّهُ مِنَ الْمُتَّقِينَ) (٢٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نَبَأَ ابْنَيْ آدَمَ): the hamza in «ابْنَيْ» is a connecting hamza (hamzat waṣl), as it is in the singular; as for the hamza of أبناء in the plural, it is a disjunctive hamza (hamzat qaṭʿ), because it arises for the plural. (إِذْ قَرَّبَا): an adverb (ẓarf) of «نَبَأَ», or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it; it cannot be an adverb of «اتْلُ». And بالحق is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «اتْلُ», that is: truthfully or veraciously. (قُرْبَانًا): it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun) and has occurred here in the position of the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The underlying form is "when they offered two offerings", but it was not put in the dual because the maṣdar is not put in the dual. Abū ʿAlī said: its implied form is "when each one of them offered an offering", as in His saying (فَاجْلِدُوهُمْ ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً), that is, each one of them. (قَالَ لَأَقْتُلَنَّكَ): that is, the one whose offering was rejected said to the one from whom it was accepted. The object of (يَتَقَبَّلُ) is omitted, that is: He accepts from the God-fearing their offerings and their deeds.

ukberi-tibyan:96-96.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ صَيْدُ الْبَحْرِ وَطَعَامُهُ مَتَاعًا لَكُمْ وَلِلسَّيَّارَةِ وَحُرِّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ صَيْدُ الْبَرِّ مَا دُمْتُمْ حُرُمًا وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ) (٩٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَطَعَامُهُ): the hāʾ is the pronoun of الْبَحْرِ; it is also said: it is the pronoun of الصَّيْدِ, and the implied wording is "and your feeding yourselves with the game". The meaning is that He made lawful for them hunting in the sea and eating what is caught in it, unlike hunting on land. (مَتَاعًا): a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); it is also said: a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "you have been given enjoyment of that, an enjoyment". (مَا دُمْتُمْ): it is read with ḍamma on the dāl, and that is the original, and with kasra on it, which is a dialect; one says دِمْتُ تُدَامُ. (حُرُمًا): plural of حَرَامٌ, like كِتَابٌ and كُتُبٌ. And it was read in an irregular (shādhdh) reading as حَرَمًا with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ and the rāʾ, i.e. "possessing ḥaram", i.e. iḥrām. It is also said: He made them as the place from which one is barred.
[Translator's note: the source text prints دُمْتُ تُدَامُ, whereas the kasra dialect it is illustrating would be دِمْتُ تُدَامُ; the vowelling is translated as the dialect described.]

ukberi-tibyan:97-97.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (جَعَلَ اللَّهُ الْكَعْبَةَ الْبَيْتَ الْحَرَامَ قِيَامًا لِلنَّاسِ وَالشَّهْرَ الْحَرَامَ وَالْهَدْيَ وَالْقَلَائِدَ ذَلِكَ لِتَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ) (٩٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جَعَلَ اللَّهُ): it has the meaning of صَيَّرَ ("made into"), so (قِيَامًا) is a second object; it is also said: it has the meaning of خَلَقَ ("created"), so قِيَامًا is a ḥāl (circumstantial). And (الْبَيْتَ): a badal (substitute) for الْكَعْبَةَ. And (قِيَامًا) is read with alif, i.e. "a cause for the upholding of their religion and their livelihood". And it is read (قِيَمًا) without alif, and it is shortened from قِيَامٌ, like خِيَمٌ for خِيَامٌ. (ذَلِكَ): in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "the ruling we have mentioned is that", i.e. and nothing else; the omitted element may also be the khabar; and it may be in the position of the accusative, i.e. "We did that" or "We legislated (that)". The lām in «لِتَعْلَمُوا» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the omitted element.

ukberi-tibyan:101-101.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَسْأَلُوا عَنْ أَشْيَاءَ إِنْ تُبْدَ لَكُمْ تَسُؤْكُمْ وَإِنْ تَسْأَلُوا عَنْهَا حِينَ يُنَزَّلُ الْقُرْآنُ تُبْدَ لَكُمْ عَفَا اللَّهُ عَنْهَا وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ) (١٠١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَنْ أَشْيَاءَ): its original form according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh is «شَيْئَاءُ», with two hamzas with an alif between them; it is of the pattern faʿlāʾ from the root of شَيْءٌ, and its second hamza is for the feminine; it is singular in form and plural in meaning, like قَصْبَاءُ ("reed-bed") and طَرْفَاءُ ("tamarisk grove"). Because of the feminine hamza it is a diptote. Then the first hamza, which is the final radical (lām) of the word, was moved forward and placed before the shīn, out of dislike of two hamzas with an alif between them, especially after the yāʾ; so its pattern became lafʿāʾ. This is a sound view, against which no difficulty arises.
Al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ said: the original of the word is شَيِّءٌ, like هَيِّنٌ, on the pattern fayʿil; then its yāʾ was lightened, as the yāʾ of هَيْنٌ was lightened, so شَيْءٌ was said, as «هَيْنٌ» was said. Then it was given the plural pattern afʿilāʾ, and the original was أَشْيِئَاءُ, as they said هَيْنٌ and أَهْوِنَاءُ; then the first hamza was dropped, so its pattern became afʿāʾ, and its final radical is dropped. [Translator's note: the printed text has «شَيْءٌ» and «أَشْيَاءَ» for the two original forms; the forms شَيِّءٌ and أَشْيِئَاءُ are what the argument requires.]
Others said: the original of «شَيْءٌ» is شَيِيءٌ, like صَدِيقٌ, then it was given the plural afʿilāʾ, like أَصْدِقَاءُ and أَنْبِيَاءُ, then the first hamza was dropped. It is also said: it is the plural of شَيْءٌ without any change, like بَيْتٌ and أَبْيَاتٌ; this is a mistake, because a plural like this is fully declinable, while on the first views it is a diptote because of the feminine hamza; had it been afʿāl it would be declinable, and أَشْيَاءُ has never been heard as declinable at all. There is long discussion of this question, and its place is morphology (al-taṣrīf). (إِنْ تُبْدَ لَكُمْ تَسُؤْكُمْ): the condition and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) are in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of أَشْيَاءَ. (عَفَا اللَّهُ عَنْهَا): it is said: it is resumptive.
And it is said: it too is in the position of the genitive, and it is intended to be placed earlier, i.e. "about things which Allah has pardoned for you".

ukberi-tibyan:102-102.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَدْ سَأَلَهَا قَوْمٌ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ ثُمَّ أَصْبَحُوا بِهَا كَافِرِينَ) (١٠٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ): it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to سَأَلَهَا; it may not be a naʿt (adjective) of قَوْمٌ nor a ḥāl (circumstantial), because an adverb of time is not an adjective of a concrete entity, nor a ḥāl from it, nor a khabar (predicate) of it.

ukberi-tibyan:103-103.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَا جَعَلَ اللَّهُ مِنْ بَحِيرَةٍ وَلَا سَائِبَةٍ وَلَا وَصِيلَةٍ وَلَا حَامٍ وَلَكِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ وَأَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ) (١٠٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا جَعَلَ اللَّهُ مِنْ بَحِيرَةٍ): «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), and جَعَلَ here has the meaning of سَمَّى ("named"); on this view بَحِيرَةٌ is one of the two objects and the other is omitted, i.e. "Allah has not named any animal a baḥīra". And جَعَلَ may be transitive to a single object, with the meaning "He did not legislate, nor institute". بَحِيرَةٌ is of the pattern faʿīla with the meaning of mafʿūla (passive); السَّائِبَةُ is of the pattern fāʿila from سَابَ يَسِيبُ, when it runs freely, and it is the reflexive (muṭāwiʿ) of سَيَّبَهُ فَسَابَ ("he let it loose and it roamed"). It is also said: it is fāʿila with the meaning of mafʿūla, i.e. مُسَيَّبَةٌ ("let loose"). الْوَصِيلَةُ has the meaning of الْوَاصِلَةُ ("the one that connects"), and الْحَامِي is an active participle from حَمَى ظَهْرَهُ يَحْمِيهِ ("he protected his back").

ukberi-tibyan:104-104.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ تَعَالَوْا إِلَى مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ وَإِلَى الرَّسُولِ قَالُوا حَسْبُنَا مَا وَجَدْنَا عَلَيْهِ آبَاءَنَا أَوَلَوْ كَانَ آبَاؤُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ شَيْئًا وَلَا يَهْتَدُونَ) (١٠٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حَسْبُنَا): it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) with the meaning of an active participle, and «مَا وَجَدْنَا» is the khabar (predicate). (وَمَا): with the meaning of الَّذِي, or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa); the implied wording is "what suffices us is that which we found". وَجَدْنَا here may have the meaning of عَلِمْنَا ("we knew"), so «عَلَيْهِ» is the second object; and it may have the meaning of صَادَفْنَا ("we came upon"), so it is transitive to a single object by itself. On this view there are two views on عَلَيْهِ. First: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb, making it transitive, as ضَرَبْتُ زَيْدًا بِالسَّوْطِ ("I struck Zayd with the whip") is extended. Second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْآبَاءِ. The answer of (أَوَلَوْ كَانَ) is omitted, its implied form being "even if they were, would they follow them?"

ukberi-tibyan:105-105.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ لَا يَضُرُّكُمْ مَنْ ضَلَّ إِذَا اهْتَدَيْتُمْ إِلَى اللَّهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ جَمِيعًا فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ) (١٠٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ): عَلَيْكُمْ here is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl), and by it «أَنْفُسَكُمْ» is in the accusative; the implied wording is "guard yourselves". The kāf and mīm in عَلَيْكُمْ are in the position of the genitive, because the verbal noun is the preposition with its genitive noun, and عَلَى alone has not been used as a verbal noun; unlike رُوَيْدَكُمْ, for the kāf and mīm there are for address only and have no position, because رُوَيْدًا has been used as a noun of command for the one addressed without the kāf of address. Similarly His saying (مَكَانَكُمْ أَنْتُمْ وَشُرَكَاؤُكُمْ): the kāf and mīm are in the position of the genitive too, and it will be mentioned in its place, if Allah the Exalted wills. (لَا يَضُرُّكُمْ): it is read with shadda and ḍamma, on the view that it is resumptive. It is also said: it ought to be jussive as the answer of the command, but it was given ḍamma to harmonise with the ḍamma of the ḍād. And it is read with fatḥa on the rāʾ, on the view that it ought to be jussive and was given fatḥa. And it is read with the rāʾ unshadded and quiescent, with kasra on the ḍād [Translator's note: i.e. لَا يَضِرْكُمْ], and it is from ضَارَهُ يَضِيرُهُ ("it harmed him"); and it is read the same way except with ḍamma on the ḍād [Translator's note: i.e. لَا يَضُرْكُمْ], and it is from ضَارَهُ يَضُورُهُ; all of these are dialectal variants of it. And (إِذَا): an adverb for يَضُرُّ; it is far-fetched that it is an adverb for ضَلَّ, because the meaning is not sound with that.

ukberi-tibyan:106-106.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا شَهَادَةُ بَيْنِكُمْ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ حِينَ الْوَصِيَّةِ اثْنَانِ ذَوَا عَدْلٍ مِنْكُمْ أَوْ آخَرَانِ مِنْ غَيْرِكُمْ إِنْ أَنْتُمْ ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَأَصَابَتْكُمْ مُصِيبَةُ الْمَوْتِ تَحْبِسُونَهُمَا مِنْ بَعْدِ الصَّلَاةِ فَيُقْسِمَانِ بِاللَّهِ إِنِ ارْتَبْتُمْ لَا نَشْتَرِي بِهِ ثَمَنًا وَلَوْ كَانَ ذَا قُرْبَى وَلَا نَكْتُمُ شَهَادَةَ اللَّهِ إِنَّا إِذًا لَمِنَ الْآثِمِينَ) (١٠٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (شَهَادَةُ بَيْنِكُمْ): it is read with الشَّهَادَةُ in the nominative and in genitive construct with بَيْنِكُمْ. The nominative is as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the genitive construct here with «بَيْنِ» is on the basis that بَيْنَ is made a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); and the khabar (predicate) is «اثْنَانِ»; the implied wording is "the testimony of two".
It is also said: the implied wording is "those who hold the testimony among you are two", the first muḍāf having been dropped; on this view «إِذَا حَضَرَ» is an adverb for الشَّهَادَةُ. As for «حِينَ الْوَصِيَّةِ», on this view there are three views on it. First: it is an adverb for الْمَوْتُ. Second: an adverb for حَضَرَ, and that is permitted since the meaning is "the causes of death have come". Third: that it is a badal (substitute) for إِذَا. It is also said: «شَهَادَةُ بَيْنِكُمْ» is a mubtadaʾ and its khabar is «إِذَا حَضَرَ», and «حِينَ» is according to the three views in i'rab.
It is also said: the khabar of الشَّهَادَةُ is حِينَ, and إِذَا is an adverb for الشَّهَادَةُ. «إِذَا» may not be the khabar of الشَّهَادَةُ with حِينَ as an adverb for it, since that would separate the maṣdar (verbal noun) from its ṣila by its khabar. Nor may الْوَصِيَّةُ govern إِذَا, because a maṣdar does not govern what precedes it, nor does a muḍāf ilayhi in i'rab govern what precedes it. If you make the adverb the khabar of الشَّهَادَةُ, then اثْنَانِ is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the two witnesses are two".
It is also said: الشَّهَادَةُ is a mubtadaʾ, and إِذَا and حِينَ are not two predicates; rather they are adverbial as we have mentioned, and اثْنَانِ is the fāʿil (agent) of «شَهَادَةُ», and the agent suffices in place of the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.
And (ذَوَا عَدْلٍ): a naʿt (adjective) of اثْنَانِ, and likewise «مِنْكُمْ». (أَوْ آخَرَانِ): conjoined to اثْنَانِ. And (مِنْ غَيْرِكُمْ): a naʿt of آخَرَانِ.
And (إِنْ أَنْتُمْ ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ): parenthetical between آخَرَانِ and its naʿt, which is «تَحْبِسُونَهُمَا», i.e. "or two others not of you, detained". And «مِنْ بَعْدِ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to تَحْبِسُونَ. And أَنْتُمْ is in the nominative as the fāʿil of an omitted verb, because it occurs after the conditional إِنْ and so cannot be nominative as a mubtadaʾ. The implied wording is "if you travelled"; when the verb was dropped, the pronoun had to be made detached, so it became أَنْتُمْ so as to stand by itself; and ضَرَبْتُمْ is an explanation of the omitted verb and has no grammatical position.
«فَيُقْسِمَانِ» is a clause conjoined to تَحْبِسُونَهُمَا. And (إِنِ ارْتَبْتُمْ): parenthetical between يُقْسِمَانِ and its answer, which is «لَا نَشْتَرِي». The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted in both places, the meaning of the speech making it unnecessary; the implied wording is "if you are in doubt, then detain them" or "then make them swear", and "if you travel in the land, then take two as witnesses". (وَلَا نَكْتُمُ): the answer of يُقْسِمَانِ, because it stands in place of the oath. [Translator's note: so in the source; the context suggests لَا نَشْتَرِي is meant here, since وَلَا نَكْتُمُ is treated below as conjoined to لَا نَشْتَرِي.]
The hāʾ in «بِهِ» refers back to Allah the Exalted, or to the oath (al-qasam), or the oath (al-yamīn), or the swearing, or to the distortion of the testimony, or to the testimony, because it is speech. And (ثَمَنًا): the object of نَشْتَرِي, and there is no omission in it, because a price is bought just as things are bought with it.
It is also said: the implied wording is "something having a price". (وَلَوْ كَانَ ذَا قُرْبَى): i.e. "even if the one testified for were…" [Translator's note: the sentence breaks off in the source.]
(وَلَا نَكْتُمُ): conjoined to لَا نَشْتَرِي. He put الشَّهَادَةَ in genitive construct with اللَّهِ because He commanded it, so it became His. And it is read «شَهَادَةً» with tanwīn (nunation), and أَللَّهِ with the hamza disjunctive (qaṭʿ) without lengthening and with kasra on the hāʾ, on the view that it is in the genitive by an omitted particle of oath, and the hamza was made disjunctive to signal that.
It is also said: its being disjunctive is a compensation for the particle of oath. And it is read the same way except with the hamza conjunctive (waṣl), the genitive being for the oath without compensation or signal.
And it is read the same way except with the hamza disjunctive and lengthened [Translator's note: i.e. آللَّهِ], the hamza on this view being a compensation for the particle of oath. And it is read with الشَّهَادَةُ given tanwīn, the hamza conjunctive, and the name of Allah in the accusative without lengthening, on the view that it is accusative by an omitted verb of oath.

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ تَبُوءَ بِإِثْمِي وَإِثْمِكَ فَتَكُونَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النَّارِ وَذَلِكَ جَزَاءُ الظَّالِمِينَ) (٢٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِإِثْمِي وَإِثْمِكَ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is: you return bearing the two sins.

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَطَوَّعَتْ لَهُ نَفْسُهُ قَتْلَ أَخِيهِ فَقَتَلَهُ فَأَصْبَحَ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ) (٣٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَطَوَّعَتْ): the majority read it with the wāw doubled, and it is read «طَاوَعَتْ», with alif and without doubling; they are two dialectal forms, and the meaning is "made [it] seem attractive". Some people said that طاوعت is transitive without lām, but this is a mistake, because the one that is transitive without lām is transitive to a single object, and here He has made it transitive to «قَتْلَ أَخِيهِ». It has also been said that the implied form is "his soul complied with him in killing his brother" (طاوعته نفسه على قتل أخيه), so He added the lām and dropped على.

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ غُرَابًا يَبْحَثُ فِي الْأَرْضِ لِيُرِيَهُ كَيْفَ يُوَارِي سَوْأَةَ أَخِيهِ قَالَ يَا وَيْلَتَا أَعَجَزْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِثْلَ هَذَا الْغُرَابِ فَأُوَارِيَ سَوْأَةَ أَخِي فَأَصْبَحَ مِنَ النَّادِمِينَ) (٣١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَيْفَ يُوَارِي): كيف is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in يواري, and the clause is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) governed by يُري. In السوأة the hamza may be lightened by casting its vowel onto the wāw, so that سَوَاةَ أخيه remains; and the wāw is not changed into alif on account of its being vowelled and preceded by fatḥa, because its vowel is accidental. The alif in (وَيْلَتَى) is a substitute for the yāʾ of the first person, and the meaning is: "O my woe, come — this is your time!" (فَأُوَارِيَ): conjoined to «أَكُونَ». Some mentioned that it may be accusative as the answer to the question, but this is nothing, since the meaning is not "would there be inability on my part, and so concealing?" Do you not see that your saying "Where is your house, so that I may visit you?" means "if I knew, I would visit", whereas the meaning here is not "if I were unable, I would conceal"?

ukberi-tibyan:32-32.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (مِنْ أَجْلِ ذَلِكَ كَتَبْنَا عَلَى بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ أَنَّهُ مَنْ قَتَلَ نَفْسًا بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ أَوْ فَسَادٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ النَّاسَ جَمِيعًا وَمَنْ أَحْيَاهَا فَكَأَنَّمَا أَحْيَا النَّاسَ جَمِيعًا وَلَقَدْ جَاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُنَا بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ ثُمَّ إِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنْهُمْ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فِي الْأَرْضِ لَمُسْرِفُونَ) (٣٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ أَجْلِ): من is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «كَتَبْنَا»; it is not attached to النادمين, because beginning with كتبنا here would not be good. The hāʾ in (إِنَّهُ) is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). And (مَنْ) is conditional. And (بِغَيْرِ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in قتل, that is: whoever kills a soul wrongfully. (أَوْ فَسَادٍ): conjoined to نفس. In an irregular (shādhdh) reading it has been read in the accusative, that is: "or did corruption", or "corrupted with corruption", that is, إفسادًا; so it was put in the place of the maṣdar (verbal noun), like العطاء. And (بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ) is an adverb (ẓarf) of «مُسْرِفُونَ», and the lām of emphasis does not prevent that.

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّمَا جَزَاءُ الَّذِينَ يُحَارِبُونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَيَسْعَوْنَ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَسَادًا أَنْ يُقَتَّلُوا أَوْ يُصَلَّبُوا أَوْ تُقَطَّعَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَرْجُلُهُمْ مِنْ خِلَافٍ أَوْ يُنْفَوْا مِنَ الْأَرْضِ ذَلِكَ لَهُمْ خِزْيٌ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَلَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ) (٣٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُحَارِبُونَ اللَّهَ): that is, the friends (awliyāʾ) of Allah; the muḍāf has been omitted.
And (أَنْ يُقَتَّلُوا) is the khabar (predicate) of «جَزَاءُ», and likewise what is conjoined to it.
They have also been read without doubling.
And (مِنْ خِلَافٍ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الأيدي and الأرجل, that is: on opposite sides.
(أَوْ يُنْفَوْا مِنَ الْأَرْضِ): that is, from the land in which they wish to reside; the adjective has been omitted. And (ذَلِكَ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject). And (لَهُمْ خِزْيٌ) is a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the khabar of ذلك. And (فِي الدُّنْيَا) is an adjective (ṣifa) of «خِزْيٌ», and it may be an adverb (ẓarf) of it. خزي may also be the khabar of ذلك, with لهم an adjective placed first, so that it is a ḥāl; and في الدنيا may be an adverb of the [implied] being-settled (istiqrār).

ukberi-tibyan:34-34.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تَابُوا مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَقْدِرُوا عَلَيْهِمْ فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) (٣٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ): an exception from «الَّذِينَ يُحَارِبُونَ», in the position of the accusative (naṣb).
It has also been said that it may be in the position of the nominative (rafʿ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the pronoun referring to it from the khabar (predicate) omitted, that is: «فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ» to them and «رَحِيمٌ» towards them.

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَابْتَغُوا إِلَيْهِ الْوَسِيلَةَ وَجَاهِدُوا فِي سَبِيلِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ) (٣٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَيْهِ الْوَسِيلَةَ): إلى may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to ابتغوا, or attached to الوسيلة, because الوسيلة is in the sense of "that by which one seeks to draw near", so it governs what precedes it. It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is: the means being towards Him.
