ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْ أَنَّ لَهُمْ مَا فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا وَمِثْلَهُ مَعَهُ لِيَفْتَدُوا بِهِ مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ مَا تُقُبِّلَ مِنْهُمْ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ) (٣٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ): العذاب is a noun for التعذيب (punishing), and it has its rule in governing; its annexation to يوم has taken «يومًا» out of adverbial use (ẓarfiyya).

ukberi-tibyan:38-38.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَالسَّارِقُ وَالسَّارِقَةُ فَاقْطَعُوا أَيْدِيَهُمَا جَزَاءً بِمَا كَسَبَا نَكَالًا مِنَ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ) (٣٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالسَّارِقُ وَالسَّارِقَةُ): a mubtadaʾ (subject). There are two views on the khabar (predicate). The first: it is omitted,
its implied form according to Sībawayh being: "and among what is recited to you [is the ruling on the thief]". According to him «فَاقْطَعُوا» cannot be the khabar because of the fāʾ; that is only permissible when the mubtadaʾ is [a relative] that you have joined to a verb or an adverbial phrase, because it then resembles a condition, and السارق is not like that. The second: the khabar is فاقطعوا أيديهما, because the alif and lām in السارق are equivalent to الذي, no particular thief being meant by it. (وَأَيْدِيَهُمَا): in the sense of يديهما (their two hands), because what is cut off from the male and female thief is their right hands; so the plural has been put in place of the dual, because a person has only one right hand, and in whatever is of this kind the plural is put in place of the dual. It may also come out according to the basic form, and both have come in a single verse; the poet said:
وَمَهْمَهَيْنِ فَدْفَدَيْنِ مَرَّتَيْنِ ... ظَهَرَاهُمَا مِثْلُ ظُهُورِ التُّرْسَيْنِ
(And two barren wastes, two rugged plains, [crossed] twice, whose two backs are like the backs of two shields.)
(جَزَاءً): a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or a maṣdar (verbal noun) of an omitted verb, that is: He requited them with a requital; and likewise «نَكَالًا».

ukberi-tibyan:107-107.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِنْ عُثِرَ عَلَى أَنَّهُمَا اسْتَحَقَّا إِثْمًا فَآخَرَانِ يَقُومَانِ مَقَامَهُمَا مِنَ الَّذِينَ اسْتَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الْأَوْلَيَانِ فَيُقْسِمَانِ بِاللَّهِ لَشَهَادَتُنَا أَحَقُّ مِنْ شَهَادَتِهِمَا وَمَا اعْتَدَيْنَا إِنَّا إِذًا لَمِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ) (١٠٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَإِنْ عُثِرَ): its maṣdar (verbal noun) is الْعُثُورُ, and its meaning is "it was discovered"; as for the maṣdar of عَثَرَ ("he stumbled") in his walking, his speech and his opinion, it is الْعِثَارُ. And (عَلَى أَنَّهُمَا): in the position of the nominative, because it stands in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)). (فَآخَرَانِ): the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "then the two witnesses are two others".
It is also said: the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb, i.e. "then let two others testify". It is also said: it is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is «يَقُومَانِ», and beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted here because a useful meaning results from it.
It is also said: the khabar is «الْأَوْلَيَانِ». It is also said: the mubtadaʾ is الْأَوْلَيَانِ and آخَرَانِ is a khabar placed first, and يَقُومَانِ is a naʿt (adjective) of آخَرَانِ, if you do not make it the khabar. And (مَقَامَهُمَا): a maṣdar. And (مِنَ الَّذِينَ): another naʿt of آخَرَانِ.
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in «يَقُومَانِ». (اسْتَحَقَّ): it is read with fatḥa on the tāʾ, with the agent named (active), and the agent is الْأَوْلَيَانِ, and the object is omitted, i.e. "their bequest". And it is read with ḍamma on it, as a passive (what has not had its agent named); and there are two views on the agent [Translator's note: i.e. the deputy agent]. First: the pronoun of الْإِثْمُ, because it was mentioned before in His saying «اسْتَحَقَّا إِثْمًا», i.e. "the sin was incurred against them".
Second: الْأَوْلَيَانِ, i.e. "the sin of the two nearest". And on «عَلَيْهِمُ» there are three views. First: it is in its usual sense, as when you say وَجَبَ عَلَيْهِ الْإِثْمُ ("the sin became binding on him").
Second: it has the meaning of فِي, i.e. "the bequest and the like became due among them".
Third: it has the meaning of مِنْ, i.e. "the two nearest claimed from them".
Like it is «اكْتَالُوا عَلَى النَّاسِ يَسْتَوْفُونَ», i.e. "from people". (الْأَوْلَيَانِ): it is read with alif as the dual of أَوْلَى, and on its nominative there are five views. First: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are the two nearest". Second: it is a mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is آخَرَانِ, and this has been mentioned. Third: it is the fāʿil of اسْتَحَقَّ, and this too has been mentioned. Fourth: it is a badal (substitute) for the pronoun in يَقُومَانِ. Fifth: that it is a naʿt of آخَرَانِ, because, although it is indefinite, it has been qualified, and by الْأَوْلَيَانِ two specific individuals are not intended; this is reported from al-Akhfash.
And it is read الْأَوَّلِينَ, which is the plural of أَوَّلُ, and it is a naʿt of الَّذِينَ اسْتَحَقَّ, or a badal for the pronoun in عَلَيْهِمْ.
And it is read الْأُولَيَيْنِ, which is the plural of أُولَى, and its i'rab is like the i'rab of الْأَوَّلِينَ.
And it is read «الْأَوَّلَانِ», the dual of الْأَوَّلُ, and its i'rab is like the i'rab of الْأَوْلَيَانِ.
[Translator's note: the printed text writes «تَثْنِيَةِ أُولَى» for the dual of أَوْلَى, «الْأُولَيِينَ» and «الْأُولَيَانِ»; the forms are rendered here as the argument requires.]
(فَيُقْسِمَانِ): conjoined to يَقُومَانِ. (لَشَهَادَتُنَا أَحَقُّ): a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and it is the answer of «يُقْسِمَانِ».

ukberi-tibyan:108-108.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكَ أَدْنَى أَنْ يَأْتُوا بِالشَّهَادَةِ عَلَى وَجْهِهَا أَوْ يَخَافُوا أَنْ تُرَدَّ أَيْمَانٌ بَعْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاسْمَعُوا وَاللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْفَاسِقِينَ) (١٠٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ذَلِكَ أَدْنَى أَنْ يَأْتُوا): i.e. "than that they should bring", or "to their bringing"; its parallels have been mentioned. And (عَلَى وَجْهِهَا): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الشَّهَادَةِ, i.e. "verified" or "sound". (أَوْ يَخَافُوا): conjoined to يَأْتُوا. And (بَعْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ): an adverb for تُرَدَّ, or a naʿt (adjective) of أَيْمَانٌ.

ukberi-tibyan:109-109.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُ اللَّهُ الرُّسُلَ فَيَقُولُ مَاذَا أُجِبْتُمْ قَالُوا لَا عِلْمَ لَنَا إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ) (١٠٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُ اللَّهُ): what governs «يَوْمَ» is «يَهْدِي», i.e. "He will not guide them on that day to an argument, or to the path of Paradise".
It is also said: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the implied wording is "and hear the account of «يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُ اللَّهُ الرُّسُلَ»", the muḍāf having been dropped. (مَاذَا): in the position of the accusative governed by «أَجَبْتُمْ», with the preposition omitted, i.e. "with what did you answer?" [Translator's note: the source writes the verb as active «أَجَبْتُمْ», whereas the verse has the passive أُجِبْتُمْ.]
مَا and ذَا here count as a single noun; it is weak to make «ذَا» have the meaning of الَّذِي here, because there is no returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) here, and dropping the returning pronoun together with a preposition is weak.
(إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ) and (إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ) are like (إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَلِيمُ الْحَكِيمُ), which has been mentioned in al-Baqara.

ukberi-tibyan:110-110.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذْ قَالَ اللَّهُ يَا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ اذْكُرْ نِعْمَتِي عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَى وَالِدَتِكَ إِذْ أَيَّدْتُكَ بِرُوحِ الْقُدُسِ تُكَلِّمُ النَّاسَ فِي الْمَهْدِ وَكَهْلًا وَإِذْ عَلَّمْتُكَ الْكِتَابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ وَالتَّوْرَاةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ وَإِذْ تَخْلُقُ مِنَ الطِّينِ كَهَيْئَةِ الطَّيْرِ بِإِذْنِي فَتَنْفُخُ فِيهَا فَتَكُونُ طَيْرًا بِإِذْنِي وَتُبْرِئُ الْأَكْمَهَ وَالْأَبْرَصَ بِإِذْنِي وَإِذْ تُخْرِجُ الْمَوْتَى بِإِذْنِي وَإِذْ كَفَفْتُ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ عَنْكَ إِذْ جِئْتَهُمْ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ فَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْهُمْ إِنْ هَذَا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ) (١١٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ قَالَ اللَّهُ): it may be a badal (substitute) for «يَوْمَ», and the implied wording is "when He will say"; «إِذْ», which is for the past, occurs here by way of narrating the situation as present (ḥikāyat al-ḥāl). And the implied wording may be "remember when He will say". (يَاعِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ): the alif of عِيسَى may carry a fatḥa, because it has been qualified by ابْنٌ and it lies between two proper names; and it may carry a ḍamma. It is like your saying يَا زَيْدُ بْنَ عُمَرَ, with fatḥa or ḍamma on the dāl. If you assume the ḍamma, it is permitted to make «ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ» a naʿt (adjective), an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) and a badal.
(إِذْ أَيَّدْتُكَ): what governs إِذْ is «نِعْمَتِي». It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from نِعْمَتِي, and it may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa). أَيَّدْتُكَ and آيَدْتُكَ: both have been read, and this has been mentioned in al-Baqara. (تُكَلِّمُ النَّاسَ): in the position of a ḥāl from the kāf in «أَيَّدْتُكَ».
And (فِي الْمَهْدِ): an adverb for «تُكَلِّمُ», or a ḥāl from the agent pronoun in «تُكَلِّمُ».
(وَكَهْلًا): also a ḥāl from it; and it may be from the kāf in أَيَّدْتُكَ, and it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara). «وَإِذْ عَلَّمْتُكَ», «وَإِذْ تَخْلُقُ» and «وَإِذْ تَخْرُجُ» are conjoined to إِذْ أَيَّدْتُكَ.
(مِنَ الطِّينِ): it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «تَخْلُقُ», so مِنْ marks the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya) of the creating; and it may be a ḥāl from «هَيْئَةِ الطَّيْرِ», on the view of those who permit placing the ḥāl of a genitive noun before it. The kāf is the object of تَخْلُقُ. We have spoken about His saying «هَيْئَةِ الطَّيْرِ» in Āl ʿImrān. (فَتَكُونُ طَيْرًا): it is read with a quiescent yāʾ without alif, and there are two views on it. First: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of an active participle.
Second: that its original is طَيِّرٌ, like سَيِّدٌ, then it was lightened; however, that is rare in words whose middle radical is yāʾ, though it is permissible. And it is read طَائِرًا, which is an adjective that has come to be used as a noun (ṣifa ghāliba).
It is also said: it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ), like الْحَامِلُ and الْبَاقِرُ. [Translator's note: so in the source; the usual examples are الْجَامِلُ ("herd of camels") and الْبَاقِرُ ("herd of cattle").] And (تُبْرِئُ): conjoined to «تَخْلُقُ». (إِذْ جِئْتَهُمْ): an adverb for كَفَفْتُ. (سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ): it is read without alif, as a maṣdar, and it points to the signs he brought.
And it is read سَاحِرٌ with alif, and it points to ʿĪsā.
It is also said: it is an active participle in the sense of a maṣdar, as they said عَائِذًا بِاللَّهِ مِنْكَ ("seeking refuge with Allah from you"), i.e. عَوْذًا or عِيَاذًا.

ukberi-tibyan:111-111.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ أَوْحَيْتُ إِلَى الْحَوَارِيِّينَ أَنْ آمِنُوا بِي وَبِرَسُولِي قَالُوا آمَنَّا وَاشْهَدْ بِأَنَّنَا مُسْلِمُونَ) (al-Māʾida: ١١١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِذْ أَوْحَيْتُ): conjoined to «إِذْ أَيَّدْتُكَ».
(أَنْ آمِنُوا): أَنْ may be maṣdariyya (infinitival), so it is in the position of the accusative governed by أَوْحَيْتُ; and it may have the meaning of أَيْ ("that is", explicative); I have mentioned its parallels.

ukberi-tibyan:112-112.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذْ قَالَ الْحَوَارِيُّونَ يَا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ رَبُّكَ أَنْ يُنَزِّلَ عَلَيْنَا مَائِدَةً مِنَ السَّمَاءِ قَالَ اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ) (١١٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ قَالَ الْحَوَارِيُّونَ): i.e. "remember when they said"; and it may be an adverb for «مُسْلِمُونَ». (هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ رَبُّكَ): it is read with yāʾ, as a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the meaning is "is your Lord able", or "will He do". It is also said: the implied wording is "will your Lord comply", and the two have one meaning, like اسْتَجَابَ and أَجَابَ, and اسْتَجِبْ and أَجِبْ. And it is read with tāʾ, with رَبَّكَ in the accusative, and the implied wording is "are you able to ask your Lord", the muḍāf having been dropped.
As for His saying «أَنْ يُنَزِّلَ»: on the first reading it is the object of يَسْتَطِيعُ, and the implied wording is "to send down" (with عَلَى) or "in sending down" (with فِي). It may also need no preposition, on the view that يَسْتَطِيعُ has the meaning of يُطِيقُ ("is capable of"). On the other reading it is the object of the omitted سُؤَالَ ("asking").

ukberi-tibyan:41-41.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا أَيُّهَا الرَّسُولُ لَا يَحْزُنْكَ الَّذِينَ يُسَارِعُونَ فِي الْكُفْرِ مِنَ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا آمَنَّا بِأَفْوَاهِهِمْ وَلَمْ تُؤْمِنْ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ هَادُوا سَمَّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ سَمَّاعُونَ لِقَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ لَمْ يَأْتُوكَ يُحَرِّفُونَ الْكَلِمَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَوَاضِعِهِ يَقُولُونَ إِنْ أُوتِيتُمْ هَذَا فَخُذُوهُ وَإِنْ لَمْ تُؤْتَوْهُ فَاحْذَرُوا وَمَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ فِتْنَتَهُ فَلَنْ تَمْلِكَ لَهُ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُطَهِّرَ قُلُوبَهُمْ لَهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيَا خِزْيٌ وَلَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ) (٤١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا يَحْزُنْكَ): a prohibition. The better reading is with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the zāy; it is also read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the zāy, from أحزنني ("it grieved me"), and this is a dialectal form.
(مِنَ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا): in the position of the accusative (naṣb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in يسارعون, or from الذين يسارعون. (بِأَفْوَاهِهِمْ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to قالوا, that is: they said with their mouths "We believe". (وَلَمْ تُؤْمِنْ قُلُوبُهُمْ): the clause is a ḥāl. (وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ هَادُوا): conjoined to His saying «مِنَ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا آمَنًا». And (سَمَّاعُونَ) is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), that is: they are listeners. It has also been said that سمّاعون is a mubtadaʾ and ومن الذين هادوا is its khabar. (لِلْكَذِبِ): there are two views on it.
The first: the lām is redundant (zāʾida), its implied form being: سمّاعون الكذب ("listeners to lies"). The second: it is not redundant; the object is omitted, and the implied form is: "listeners to your reports for the sake of lying", that is, in order to lie about you in them. And the second (سَمَّاعُونَ) is a repetition of the first. And (لِقَوْمٍ) is attached to it, that is: for the sake of a people. The lām in لقوم may also be attached to الكذب, because the second سمّاعون is a repetition, and the implied form is: "in order to lie for another people". And (لَمْ يَأْتُوكَ) is in the position of the genitive (jarr), another adjective (ṣifa) of قوم. (يُحَرِّفُونَ): there are two views on it. The first: it is resumptive, with no grammatical position, or in the position of the nominative
as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is: they distort. The second: it is not resumptive; rather it is an adjective of سمّاعون, that is: listeners who distort. It may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun in سمّاعون, and it may be another adjective of قوم, that is: distorting. And (مِنْ بَعْدِ مَوَاضِعِهِ) is mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Nisāʾ. (يَقُولُونَ): like يحرّفون; it may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun in يحرّفون. (مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا): in the position of a ḥāl, the implied form being: "anything that is from the command of Allah".

ukberi-tibyan:42-42.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (سَمَّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ أَكَّالُونَ لِلسُّحْتِ فَإِنْ جَاءُوكَ فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ أَوْ أَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ وَإِنْ تُعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ فَلَنْ يَضُرُّوكَ شَيْئًا وَإِنْ حَكَمْتَ فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ بِالْقِسْطِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُقْسِطِينَ) (٤٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (سَمَّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ): that is, they are listeners; and similar to it is «أَكَّالُونَ لِلسُّحْتِ». «السُّحْتِ» and «السَّحَتِ» are two dialectal forms, and it has been read with both. (فَلَنْ يَضُرُّوكَ شَيْئًا): [شيئًا] is in the position of the maṣdar (verbal noun), that is: any harm.

ukberi-tibyan:43-43.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَكَيْفَ يُحَكِّمُونَكَ وَعِنْدَهُمُ التَّوْرَاةُ فِيهَا حُكْمُ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّوْنَ مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ وَمَا أُولَئِكَ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ) (٤٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَكَيْفَ يُحَكِّمُونَكَ): كيف is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in يحكّمونك. (وَعِنْدَهُمُ التَّوْرَاةُ): a clause in the position of a ḥāl; التوراة is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and عندهم the khabar (predicate). You may also make التوراة nominative by the adverb (ẓarf).
(فِيهَا حُكْمُ اللَّهِ): in the position of a ḥāl, and what governs it is the verbal meaning contained in «عِنْدَ»; and حكم الله is a mubtadaʾ, or governed by the adverbial phrase.

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَا التَّوْرَاةَ فِيهَا هُدًى وَنُورٌ يَحْكُمُ بِهَا النَّبِيُّونَ الَّذِينَ أَسْلَمُوا لِلَّذِينَ هَادُوا وَالرَّبَّانِيُّونَ وَالْأَحْبَارُ بِمَا اسْتُحْفِظُوا مِنْ كِتَابِ اللَّهِ وَكَانُوا عَلَيْهِ شُهَدَاءَ فَلَا تَخْشَوُا النَّاسَ وَاخْشَوْنِ وَلَا تَشْتَرُوا بِآيَاتِي ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا وَمَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْكَافِرُونَ) (٤٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِيهَا هُدًى وَنُورٌ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from التوراة. (يَحْكُمُ بِهَا النَّبِيُّونَ): a clause in [the position of] a ḥāl from the genitive pronoun in «فِيهَا». (لِلَّذِينَ هَادُوا): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يحكم. (وَالرَّبَّانِيُّونَ وَالْأَحْبَارُ): conjoined to «النَّبِيُّونَ». (بِمَا اسْتُحْفِظُوا): it may be a badal (substitute) from His saying «بِهَا» in His saying «يَحْكُمُ بِهَا»; the preposition has been repeated because of the length of the speech, and it is permissible as well even when it is not long. It has also been said that الربانيون is nominative by an omitted verb, the implied form being: "and the rabbis and the scholars judge
by what they were entrusted to preserve". It has also been said that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) «[Translator's note: so in the text; the explanation that follows ("by reason of …") suggests the bāʾ is causal.]», that is: they judge by the Torah by reason of their having been entrusted with preserving it. And «مَا» is in the sense of الذي (relative noun), that is: by what they were asked to preserve. (مِنْ كِتَابِ اللَّهِ): a ḥāl from the omitted [pronoun], or from «مَا». And (عَلَيْهِ) is attached to «شُهَدَاءَ».

ukberi-tibyan:113-113.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا نُرِيدُ أَنْ نَأْكُلَ مِنْهَا وَتَطْمَئِنَّ قُلُوبُنَا وَنَعْلَمَ أَنْ قَدْ صَدَقْتَنَا وَنَكُونَ عَلَيْهَا مِنَ الشَّاهِدِينَ) (١١٣) قَالَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّنَا أَنْزِلْ عَلَيْنَا مَائِدَةً مِنَ السَّمَاءِ تَكُونُ لَنَا عِيدًا لِأَوَّلِنَا وَآخِرِنَا وَآيَةً مِنْكَ وَارْزُقْنَا وَأَنْتَ خَيرُ الرَّازِقِينَ) (١١٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ قَدْ صَدَقْتَنَا): أَنْ is lightened from the heavy (أَنَّ), its noun is omitted, and «قَدْ» is a compensation for it.
It is also said: أَنْ is maṣdariyya (infinitival), and «قَدْ» does not prevent that.
(تَكُونُ): a naʿt (adjective) of مَائِدَةً.
And (لَنَا): it may be the khabar (predicate) of kāna, and «عِيدًا» a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the adverbial phrase, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in kāna, on the view of those who allow kāna to put a ḥāl in the accusative.
And «عِيدًا» may be the khabar; on this view there are two views on «لَنَا». First: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in تَكُونُ.
Second: that it is a ḥāl from «عِيدًا», because it is a naʿt of it placed before it.
As for «لِأَوَّلِنَا وَآخِرِنَا»: if «لَنَا» is made the khabar, or a ḥāl from the agent of تَكُونُ, then it is a naʿt of «عِيدًا»; and if «لَنَا» is made a naʿt of «عِيدًا», then لِأَوَّلِنَا وَآخِرِنَا is a badal (substitute) for the genitive pronoun, with the preposition repeated.
And it is read «لِأُولَانَا وَأُخْرَانَا», with the feminine, referring to the group or the party. As for «مِنَ السَّمَاءِ», it may be a naʿt of مَائِدَةً, and it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يُنَزِّلَ».
(وَآيَةً): conjoined to «عِيدًا». And (مِنْكَ): a naʿt of it.

ukberi-tibyan:115-115.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ اللَّهُ إِنِّي مُنَزِّلُهَا عَلَيْكُمْ فَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بَعْدُ مِنْكُمْ فَإِنِّي أُعَذِّبُهُ عَذَابًا لَا أُعَذِّبُهُ أَحَدًا مِنَ الْعَالَمِينَ) (١١٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْكُمْ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in يَكْفُرُ.
(عَذَابًا): a noun of the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar) which is التَّعْذِيبُ ("punishing"), so it occurs in its place; and it may be made a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa). As for His saying «لَا أُعَذِّبُهُ»: the hāʾ may be for the punishment, and on this view there are two views on it. First: that the preposition has been dropped, i.e. "I will not punish anyone with it".
Second: that it is a mafʿūl bihi by extension.
And it may be the pronoun of the emphatic maṣdar, as when you say ظَنَنْتُهُ زَيْدًا مُنْطَلِقًا ("I thought it, Zayd departing", i.e. I thought Zayd was departing); this hāʾ does not then refer back to the first عَذَابًا.
If you say: «لَا أُعَذِّبُهُ» is a naʿt (adjective) of عَذَابًا; so on this interpretation nothing refers back from the naʿt to what it qualifies —
it is answered: since the second occurs in place of the maṣdar, and the maṣdar is a genus, and «عَذَابًا» is indefinite, the first is included in the second, and the second encompasses the first; it is like زَيْدٌ نِعْمَ الرَّجُلُ ("Zayd, how excellent a man!").
And the hāʾ may be the pronoun of مَنْ, with an omission in the speech, i.e. "I will not punish the disbeliever", i.e. "the like of the disbeliever", i.e. "the like of the punishment of the disbeliever".

ukberi-tibyan:116-116.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ قَالَ اللَّهُ يَا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ أَأَنْتَ قُلْتَ لِلنَّاسِ اتَّخِذُونِي وَأُمِّيَ إِلَهَيْنِ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ قَالَ سُبْحَانَكَ مَا يَكُونُ لِي أَنْ أَقُولَ مَا لَيْسَ لِي بِحَقٍّ إِنْ كُنْتُ قُلْتُهُ فَقَدْ عَلِمْتَهُ تَعْلَمُ مَا فِي نَفْسِي وَلَا أَعْلَمُ مَا فِي نَفْسِكَ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ) (١١٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (اتَّخِذُونِي): this is transitive to two objects, because they [Translator's note: so in the source, i.e. the verb] have the meaning of صَيِّرُونِي ("make me into").
And (مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ): in the position of a naʿt (adjective) of إِلَهَيْنِ.
And it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to اتَّخِذُوا. (أَنْ أَقُولَ): in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of يَكُونُ, and لِي is the khabar (predicate).
And (مَا لَيْسَ): with the meaning of الَّذِي, or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa), and it is the object of أَقُولَ, because the implied wording is "that I claim" or "that I mention". The noun of لَيْسَ is latent (mustatir) in it, and its khabar is «لِي». And (بِحَقٍّ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the preposition phrase, and what governs it is the preposition phrase.
And «بِحَقٍّ» may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its implied form being "what is not established for me by reason of a right"; so the bāʾ is attached to the omitted verb, not to the preposition phrase itself, because abstract (meaning-based) governors do not govern a mafʿūl bihi. And «بِحَقٍّ» may be made the khabar of لَيْسَ, with «لِي» for clarification, as in their saying سَقْيًا لَهُ وَرَعْيًا ("may he be watered and cared for"). And «بِحَقٍّ» may be the khabar of لَيْسَ, and «لِي» a naʿt of «حَقٍّ» placed before it, so it became a ḥāl; this is construed on the view of those who permit placing the ḥāl of a genitive noun before it. (إِنْ كُنْتُ قُلْتُهُ): كُنْتُ is past in form, and the future is intended; the implied wording is "if my claim of it should prove true". What called for this is that the conditional إِنْ has meaning only in the future, so the upshot of the meaning comes to what we have mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:117-117.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَا قُلْتُ لَهُمْ إِلَّا مَا أَمَرْتَنِي بِهِ أَنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبَّكُمْ وَكُنْتُ عَلَيْهِمْ شَهِيدًا مَا دُمْتُ فِيهِمْ فَلَمَّا تَوَفَّيْتَنِي كُنْتَ أَنْتَ الرَّقِيبَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَنْتَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ) (١١٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا قُلْتُ لَهُمْ إِلَّا مَا أَمَرْتَنِي بِهِ): «مَا» is in the position of the accusative governed by قُلْتُ, i.e. "I mentioned" or "I conveyed that which You commanded me", so it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
And «مَا» may be an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa), and it is also a mafʿūl bihi.
(أَنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ): أَنْ may be maṣdariyya (infinitival), with the imperative as its ṣila. Its position has three views: the genitive, as a badal (substitute) for the hāʾ; the nominative, by implying هُوَ; and the accusative, by implying أَعْنِي ("I mean"), or as a badal from the position of بِهِ. It may not have the meaning of the explicative أَيْ, because speaking (al-qawl) has been stated explicitly, and «أَيْ» does not occur where speaking is stated explicitly. (رَبِّي): a naʿt (adjective) of اللَّهَ or a badal for it. And (عَلَيْهِمْ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to «شَهِيدًا».
(مَا دُمْتُ): «مَا» here is maṣdariyya, and the time with it is omitted, i.e. "for the duration of my remaining".
And (دُمْتُ) here may be the incomplete (nāqiṣa) one, with «فِيهِمْ» as its khabar (predicate).
And it may be the complete (tāmma) one, i.e. "as long as I stayed among them", so فِيهِمْ is an adverbial for the verb.
And (الرَّقِيبَ): the khabar of kāna. (وَأَنْتَ) [Translator's note: i.e. the أَنْتَ in كُنْتَ أَنْتَ الرَّقِيبَ]: a separating pronoun (faṣl), or a tawkīd (emphasis) of the agent.
And it is read in the nominative [Translator's note: i.e. الرَّقِيبُ], on the view that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar in the position of the accusative.

ukberi-tibyan:118-118.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنْ تُعَذِّبْهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ عِبَادُكَ وَإِنْ تَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ فَإِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ) (١١٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنْ تُعَذِّبْهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ عِبَادُكَ): the fāʾ is (introducing) the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and it is construed according to the meaning, i.e. "if You punish them, You are just, and if You forgive them, You are bountiful".

ukberi-tibyan:119-119.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ اللَّهُ هَذَا يَوْمُ يَنْفَعُ الصَّادِقِينَ صِدْقُهُمْ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ ذَلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ) (١١٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هَذَا يَوْمُ): هَذَا is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «يَوْمُ» its khabar (predicate), and it is declinable (muʿrab), because it is in genitive construct with something declinable, so it kept its right to declension. And «يَوْمَ» is read with fatḥa, and it is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf); and on this there are two views. First: it [Translator's note: i.e. هَذَا] is the object of قَالَ, i.e. "Allah said this saying on the day".
Second: that هَذَا is a mubtadaʾ, and يَوْمَ is an adverb for the omitted khabar, i.e. "this takes place" or "will be on the day (when truthfulness) benefits".
The Kufans said: «يَوْمُ» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of هَذَا, but it is indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is in genitive construct with a verb; according to them it may be made indeclinable even if it is in construct with something declinable, whereas according to us that is permitted only when it is in construct with something indeclinable. And (صِدْقُهُمْ): the fāʿil (agent) of يَنْفَعُ; and it has been read in an irregular (shādhdh) reading as «صِدْقَهُمْ» in the accusative, on the view that the agent is the pronoun of the name of Allah; and صِدْقَهُمْ in the accusative is on four views.
First: that it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), i.e. "for their truthfulness". Second: that it is with the preposition dropped, i.e. "by their truthfulness".
Third: that it is an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "those who are truthful with their truthfulness", as you say تَصْدُقُ الصِّدْقَ ("you speak the truth truly"). Fourth: that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), with the agent latent in الصَّادِقِينَ, i.e. "who are true to the truth", as in his saying صَدَقْتُهُ الْقِتَالَ ("I was true to him in fighting"), and the meaning is "they realise the truth".

ukberi-tibyan:45-45.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَكَتَبْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ فِيهَا أَنَّ النَّفْسَ بِالنَّفْسِ وَالْعَيْنَ بِالْعَيْنِ وَالْأَنْفَ بِالْأَنْفِ وَالْأُذُنَ بِالْأُذُنِ وَالسِّنَّ بِالسِّنِّ وَالْجُرُوحَ قِصَاصٌ فَمَنْ تَصَدَّقَ بِهِ فَهُوَ كَفَّارَةٌ لَهُ وَمَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ) (٤٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (النَّفْسَ بِالنَّفْسِ): بالنفس is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ) as the khabar (predicate) of أنّ, and there is a pronoun in it. As for «الْعَيْنَ» up to His saying (وَالسِّنَّ), it is read in the accusative (naṣb), conjoined to what أنّ governed, and in the nominative, and on this there are three views. The first: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the genitive phrase is its khabar, so that clauses have been conjoined to a clause. The second: that the nominative words among them are conjoined to the pronoun in His saying بالنفس, and on this view the genitive phrases are ḥāls (circumstantials) clarifying the meaning, because the nominative noun on this view is the fāʿil (agent) of the preposition [phrase]; the conjunction is permissible without emphasis, as in His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا أَشْرَكْنَا وَلَا آبَاؤُنَا). The third: that they are conjoined according to the meaning, because the meaning of «كَتَبْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ» is: We said to them: "the soul for the soul".
It may not be conjoined to «أَنَّ» and what it governs, because it, together with what it governs, is in the position of the accusative.
As for His saying «وَالْجُرُوحَ», it is read in the accusative, construed with «النَّفْسَ», and in the nominative, and on this there are the three views.
It may also be resumptive, that is: and wounds are [subject to] retaliation in the law of Muḥammad. The hāʾ in «بِهِ» refers to the retaliation.
And (فَهُوَ) is an allusion to the giving in charity, and the hāʾ in «لَهُ» refers to the one who gives in charity.

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقَفَّيْنَا عَلَى آثَارِهِمْ بِعِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ التَّوْرَاةِ وَآتَيْنَاهُ الْإِنْجِيلَ فِيهِ هُدًى وَنُورٌ وَمُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ التَّوْرَاةِ وَهُدًى وَمَوْعِظَةً لِلْمُتَّقِينَ) (٤٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: the first (مُصَدِّقًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from عيسى.
And (مِنَ التَّوْرَاةِ) is a ḥāl from «مَا», or from the pronoun in the adverbial phrase. And (فِيهِ هُدًى) is a clause in the position of a ḥāl from الإنجيل. The second (وَمُصَدِّقًا) is another ḥāl from الإنجيل; it has also been said: from عيسى as well. (وَهُدًى وَمَوْعِظَةً): a ḥāl from الإنجيل as well; it may also be from عيسى, that is: guiding and admonishing, or possessed of guidance and possessed of admonition. It may also be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), that is: We sent [him] following for the sake of guidance, or: We gave him the Gospel for the sake of guidance. In an irregular (shādhdh) reading it has been read in the nominative, that is: and in the Gospel there is guidance and admonition (هَدًى وَمَوْعِظَةً «[Translator's note: so vowelled in the text, though the reading under discussion is the nominative.]»), the guidance being repeated for emphasis.

ukberi-tibyan:47-47.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلْيَحْكُمْ أَهْلُ الْإِنْجِيلِ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فِيهِ وَمَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ) (٤٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلْيَحْكُمْ): it is read with sukūn on the lām and the mīm, as a command.
It is also read with kasra on the lām and fatḥa on the mīm, on the basis that it is the lām of purpose (lām kay), that is: and We sent [him] following so that they might believe and so that [the people of the Gospel] might judge.

ukberi-tibyan:48-48.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَأَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ بِالْحَقِّ مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ وَمُهَيْمِنًا عَلَيْهِ فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ وَلَا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْوَاءَهُمْ عَمَّا جَاءَكَ مِنَ الْحَقِّ لِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنَا مِنْكُمْ شِرْعَةً وَمِنْهَاجًا وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَجَعَلَكُمْ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً وَلَكِنْ لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ فِي مَا آتَاكُمْ فَاسْتَبِقُوا الْخَيْرَاتِ إِلَى اللَّهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ جَمِيعًا فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ) (٤٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِالْحَقِّ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الكتاب. (مُصَدِّقًا): a ḥāl from the pronoun in His saying بالحق; it cannot be a ḥāl from الكتاب, since there cannot be two ḥāls for one operator.
(وَمُهَيْمِنًا): also a ḥāl. And «مِنَ الْكِتَابِ» is a ḥāl from «مَا», or from the pronoun in the adverbial phrase, and the second «الْكِتَابِ» is generic. The original form of مهيمن is مؤيمن, because it is derived from الأمانة (trust), since المهيمن is
the witness; and there is no [root] همن in the language for the hāʾ to be radical. (عَمَّا جَاءَكَ): in the position of a ḥāl, that is: turning away from what has come to you. And (مِنَ الْحَقِّ) is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «جَاءَكَ», or from «مَا». (لِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنَا مِنْكُمْ): منكم may not be an adjective (ṣifa) of كلّ, because that would require separating the adjective from the qualified noun by an extraneous element that adds no reinforcement to the speech, and it would also require separating جعلنا from what it governs, namely «شِرْعَةً». Rather, it is attached to something omitted, its implied form being: "I mean".
As for «جَعَلْنَا» here, if you wish you may make it the one transitive to a single object, and if you wish you may make it in the sense of "We made [into]" (صيّرنا). (وَلَكِنْ لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, its implied form being: "but He divided you in order to test you". (مَرْجِعُكُمْ جَمِيعًا): [جميعًا] is a ḥāl from the genitive pronoun, and there are two views on its operator. The first: the annexed maṣdar (verbal noun), because it is in the sense of "to Him you will all be returned", and the genitive pronoun is in meaning the agent, or stands in place of the agent. The second: that it is governed by the being-settled (istiqrār) by which «مَرْجِعُكُمْ» is made nominative, or by the pronoun that is in the preposition [phrase].

ukberi-tibyan:49-49.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَأَنِ احْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ وَلَا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْوَاءَهُمْ وَاحْذَرْهُمْ أَنْ يَفْتِنُوكَ عَنْ بَعْضِ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْكَ فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَاعْلَمْ أَنَّمَا يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُصِيبَهُمْ بِبَعْضِ ذُنُوبِهِمْ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنَ النَّاسِ لَفَاسِقُونَ) (٤٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَنِ احْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ): there are two views on «أَنْ». The first: it is maṣdariyya and the imperative is its ṣila, and there are three views on its position.
The first: accusative (naṣb), conjoined to الكتاب in His saying «وَأَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ», that is: and We sent down to you the [command to] judge. The second: genitive (jarr), conjoined to «الْحَقِّ», that is: We sent down to you the Book with the truth and with the [command to] judge; on this view it may be accusative once the preposition is omitted. The third: that it is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ), its implied form being: "and that you judge between them by what Allah has sent down is Our command" or "Our word".
It has also been said that أن is in the sense of أي (explicative), but this is far-fetched, because the wāw prevents that, and the meaning spoils it, because the explicative «أَنْ» must be preceded by [a verb of] saying that it explains. This view can be made sound by taking the implied form to be "and We commanded you", and then this command is explained by احكم.
(أَنْ يَفْتِنُوكَ): there are two views on it. The first: it is a badal (substitute) from the object pronoun, a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl), that is: beware of their tempting [you]. The second: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), that is: for fear that they tempt you.

ukberi-tibyan:50-50.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَفَحُكْمَ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ يَبْغُونَ وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ مِنَ اللَّهِ حُكْمًا لِقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ) (٥٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَفَحُكْمَ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ): it is read with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ, sukūn on the kāf and fatḥa on the mīm, and what makes it accusative
is يبغون. It is also read with fatḥa on all of them, and it is then also accusative by يبغون, that is: احكم حكم الجاهلية «[Translator's note: so in the text; on this reading حَكَمَ means "judge", i.e. "the judge of the Jāhiliyya".]». And it is read تبغون, with tāʾ, as an address, because there is address before it.
It is also read with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ, sukūn on the kāf and ḍamma on the mīm, on the basis that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is يبغون, with the referring pronoun omitted, that is: يبغونه ("they seek it"). This is weak, and it has only come in poetry, except that it is not a case of poetic necessity; the verse cited as evidence for it is the saying of Abū al-Najm:
قَدْ أَصْبَحَتْ أَمُّ الْخِيَارِ تَدَّعِي ... عَلَيَّ ذَنْبًا كُلُّهُ لَمْ أَصْنَعِ
(Umm al-Khiyār has come to claim against me a sin, none of which have I committed.)
He made كلّه nominative, and had he made it accusative the metre would not have been spoiled.
(وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ): mubtadaʾ and khabar, and it is a question in the sense of negation. And (حُكْمًا) is a tamyīz (specification). And (لِقَوْمٍ): in meaning it is "in the view of a people who are certain".
The meaning is not that the judgement is for them; rather the meaning is that the one who is certain reflects on Allah's judgement, and so it is good in his view. Of this kind is (إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَةً لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ) and (لِقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ), and the like.
It has also been said that it [the lām] is in its proper sense, and the meaning is that Allah's judgement is in favour of the believers against the unbelievers; and likewise the sign is for them, that is, the proof is in their favour.

ukberi-tibyan:51-51.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَتَّخِذُوا الْيَهُودَ وَالنَّصَارَى أَوْلِيَاءَ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَاءُ بَعْضٍ وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّهُمْ مِنْكُمْ فَإِنَّهُ مِنْهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ) (٥١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَاءُ بَعْضٍ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) with no grammatical position.

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَتَرَى الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ يُسَارِعُونَ فِيهِمْ يَقُولُونَ نَخْشَى أَنْ تُصِيبَنَا دَائِرَةٌ فَعَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ بِالْفَتْحِ أَوْ أَمْرٍ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ فَيُصْبِحُوا عَلَى مَا أَسَرُّوا فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ نَادِمِينَ) (٥٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَتَرَى الَّذِينَ): it may be from seeing with the eye, in which case يسارعون is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).
It may also be in the sense of "you know", and then يسارعون is a ḥāl as well.
It may also be from seeing with the heart, which is transitive to two objects, in which case يسارعون is the second object. In an irregular (shādhdh) reading it has been read with yāʾ, the agent being Allah the Exalted. And (يَقُولُونَ) is a ḥāl from the agent pronoun in يسارعون. And (دَائِرَةٌ) is an adjective that has become predominant [as a noun], with which the qualified noun is not mentioned. (أَنْ يَأْتِيَ): in the position of the accusative (naṣb) as the khabar (predicate) of عسى. It has also been said that it is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ) as a badal (substitute) from the name of Allah. (فَيُصْبِحُوا): conjoined to يأتي.

ukberi-tibyan:53-53.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَهَؤُلَاءِ الَّذِينَ أَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ إِنَّهُمْ لَمَعَكُمْ حَبِطَتْ أَعْمَالُهُمْ فَأَصْبَحُوا خَاسِرِينَ) (٥٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَيَقُولُ): it is read in the nominative without the conjunctive wāw, and it is then resumptive. It is also read with the wāw likewise [in the nominative], and it is read with the wāw and the accusative. On the accusative there are four views. The first: that it is conjoined to يأتي, construed according to the meaning, because the meaning of "عسى الله أن يأتي" and "عسى أن يأتي الله" is the same. It may not be conjoined to the wording of أن يأتي, because أن يأتي is the khabar (predicate) of عسى and what is conjoined to it takes its ruling, so it would need a pronoun referring back to the noun of عسى, and there is no pronoun in His saying (وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا); it would then be like your saying "may Allah [be such] that those who believe say". The second: that it is conjoined to the wording of يأتي on the view in which [أن يأتي] was made a badal (substitute), so that it enters into the noun of عسى, and its khabar is dispensed with by the event that its noun contains.
The third view: that it is conjoined to the wording of يأتي while it is a khabar, and an omitted pronoun is implied with the conjoined element, its implied form being: "and those who believe say [it] because of him". The fourth: that it is conjoined to الفتح, its implied form being: "perhaps Allah will bring the victory, and [bring about] that those who believe say". (جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ): there are two views on it. The first: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it is definite here; the implied form is: "and they swore by Allah, يجهلون «[Translator's note: so in the text; evidently a slip for يجتهدون, "exerting themselves".]» the utmost of their oaths". So the ḥāl is in reality مجتهدين ("exerting themselves"); then the imperfect verb was put in its place, and then the maṣdar (verbal noun) was put in place of the verb because it indicates it. The second: that it is a maṣdar governed by أقسموا, being from its meaning, not from its wording.

ukberi-tibyan:54-54.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَنْ يَرْتَدَّ مِنْكُمْ عَنْ دِينِهِ فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِي اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ أَذِلَّةٍ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَعِزَّةٍ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ يُجَاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلَا يَخَافُونَ لَوْمَةَ لَائِمٍ ذَلِكَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ) (٥٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَنْ يَرْتَدَّ مِنْكُمْ): it is read with fatḥa on the dāl and with it doubled, by assimilation (idghām), the dāl being given fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; and it is read «يَرْتَدِدْ», with the assimilation undone and the jussive (jazm) according to the original form. (وَمِنْكُمْ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun. (يُحِبُّهُمْ): in the position of the genitive (jarr), an adjective (ṣifa) of قوم.
(وَيُحِبُّونَهُ): conjoined to it; it may also be a ḥāl from the accusative pronoun, its implied form being: "while they love Him". (أَذِلَّةٍ) and (أَعِزَّةٍ): also two adjectives. (يُجَاهِدُونَ): it may also be an adjective of قوم, and it has come without a wāw, just as «أَذِلَّةٍ» and «أَعِزَّةٍ» came; it may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «أَعِزَّةٍ», that is: they are mighty while striving; and it may be resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:55-55.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا الَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلَاةَ وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكَاةَ وَهُمْ رَاكِعُونَ) (٥٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلَاةَ): an adjective (ṣifa) of الذين آمنوا. (وَهُمْ رَاكِعُونَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in يؤتون.

ukberi-tibyan:56-56.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا فَإِنَّ حِزْبَ اللَّهِ هُمُ الْغَالِبُونَ) (٥٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَإِنَّ حِزْبَ اللَّهِ هُمُ الْغَالِبُونَ): it has been said that it is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), which is «مَنْ», and no pronoun from it refers back to it because الحزب is «مَنْ» in meaning, so it is as if He had said: "then they are the victorious".

ukberi-tibyan:57-57.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَتَّخِذُوا الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا دِينَكُمْ هُزُوًا وَلَعِبًا مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ وَالْكُفَّارَ أَوْلِيَاءَ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ) (٥٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the first «الَّذِينَ», or from the agent in «اتَّخَذُوا». (وَالْكُفَّارَ): it is read in the genitive (jarr), conjoined to the genitive الذين, and in the accusative (naṣb), conjoined to the accusative الذين; both meanings are sound.

ukberi-tibyan:58-58.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذَا نَادَيْتُمْ إِلَى الصَّلَاةِ اتَّخَذُوهَا هُزُوًا وَلَعِبًا ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ) (٥٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ): ذلك is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and what follows it is the khabar (predicate), that is: that is because of their ignorance, that is: it occurs because of their ignorance.

ukberi-tibyan:59-59.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ هَلْ تَنْقِمُونَ مِنَّا إِلَّا أَنْ آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْنَا وَمَا أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَأَنَّ أَكْثَرَكُمْ فَاسِقُونَ) (٥٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هَلْ تَنْقِمُونَ): it is read with the lām pronounced distinctly, according to the original, and with it assimilated into the tāʾ because of its closeness to it in point of articulation. «تَنْقِمُونَ» is read with kasra on the qāf and with fatḥa, and this depends on the past tense, in which there are two dialectal forms: نقِم ينقَم and نقَم ينقِم. And (مِنَّا) is the second object of تنقمون, and what comes after إلا is the first object. منّا may not be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from أن and the verb, for two reasons: first, the ḥāl would come before إلا; second, the ṣila would come before the relative. The implied form is: "do you resent anything from us except our faith?"
As for His saying «وَأَنَّ أَكْثَرَكُمْ فَاسِقُونَ», there are two views on its position.
The first: that it is conjoined to أن آمنّا, and the meaning on this view is: you resented our faith and your [own] refraining, that is, you resented our opposing you. This is like your saying to a man: "you resented nothing in me except that I am loved by people and you are hated", even though he may not admit that he is hated.
The second view: that it is conjoined to ما, and the implied form is: "except that we believe in Allah and in [the fact] that most of you are transgressors".

ukberi-tibyan:60-60.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ هَلْ أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِشَرٍّ مِنْ ذَلِكَ مَثُوبَةً عِنْدَ اللَّهِ مَنْ لَعَنَهُ اللَّهُ وَغَضِبَ عَلَيْهِ وَجَعَلَ مِنْهُمُ الْقِرَدَةَ وَالْخَنَازِيرَ وَعَبَدَ الطَّاغُوتَ أُولَئِكَ شَرٌّ مَكَانًا وَأَضَلُّ عَنْ سَوَاءِ السَّبِيلِ) (٦٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَثُوبَةً): accusative (manṣūb) as a tamyīz (specification), and what it specifies is شرّ. It is also read «مَثْوَبَةً», with sukūn on the thāʾ and fatḥa on the wāw, and it has been mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Baqara. And (عِنْدَ اللَّهِ) is an adjective (ṣifa) of «مَثُوبَةً». (مَنْ لَعَنَهُ): it is in a position on which there are three views. The first: it is in the position of the genitive (jarr) as a badal (substitute) from شرّ. The second: it is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) by a verb indicated by أنبّئكم, that is: I acquaint you with whom Allah has cursed. The third: it is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ), that is: he is the one whom Allah has cursed.
(وَعَبَدَ الطَّاغُوتَ):
it is read with fatḥa on the ʿayn and the bāʾ and with الطاغوت in the accusative, on the basis that it is a verb conjoined to لعن. It is read with fatḥa on the ʿayn and ḍamma on the bāʾ and with الطاغوت in the genitive; عَبُد here is a noun like يَقُظ and نَدُس, it has the meaning of the plural, and what follows it is genitive by its annexation to it, and it is accusative by جعل.
It is read with ḍamma on the ʿayn and the bāʾ, with fatḥa on the dāl and with what follows it in the genitive; it is the plural of عبد, like سقف and سُقُف, or of عبيد, like قتيل and قُتُل, or of عابد, like نازل and نُزُل, or of عباد, like كتاب and كُتُب, so that it is a plural of a plural, like ثمار and ثُمُر.
It is read «عُبَّدُ الطَّاغُوتِ», with ḍamma on the ʿayn and fatḥa on the bāʾ, doubled, like ضارب and ضُرَّب.
It is read «عُبَّادُ الطَّاغُوتِ», like صائم and صُوَّام.
It is read «عِبَادُ الطَّاغُوتِ», and this is clear, like صائم and صِيام.
It is read «وَعَابِدَ الطَّاغُوتِ» and «عُبَدَ الطَّاغُوتِ», on the basis that it is an adjective, like حُطَم.
It is read «وَعُبِدَ الطَّاغُوتُ», on the basis that it is a passive verb, with الطاغوت in the nominative. It is also read «وَعَبُد», like ظَرُف, that is: that became for the ṭāghūt like something innate.
It is read «وعبدوا», on the basis that it is a verb, the wāw is the agent, and الطاغوت is accusative.
And it is read «وَعَبَدَةُ الطَّاغُوتِ», which is the plural of عابد, like قاتل and قَتَلة.

ukberi-tibyan:61-61.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذَا جَاءُوكُمْ قَالُوا آمَنَّا وَقَدْ دَخَلُوا بِالْكُفْرِ وَهُمْ قَدْ خَرَجُوا بِهِ وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْتُمُونَ) (٦١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَقَدْ دَخَلُوا): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent in قالوا, or from the agent in آمنّا. And (بِالْكُفْرِ) is in the position of a ḥāl from the agent in دخلوا, that is: they entered as unbelievers. (وَهُمْ قَدْ خَرَجُوا): another ḥāl. The implied form may also be: "and they had already gone out with it".

ukberi-tibyan:62-62.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَتَرَى كَثِيرًا مِنْهُمْ يُسَارِعُونَ فِي الْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوَانِ وَأَكْلِهِمُ السُّحْتَ لَبِئْسَ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ) (٦٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَكْلِهِمُ): the maṣdar (verbal noun) is annexed to its agent, and (السُّحْتَ) is its object; similar to it is (عَنْ قَوْلِهِمُ الْإِثْمَ).

ukberi-tibyan:64-64.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقَالَتِ الْيَهُودُ يَدُ اللَّهِ مَغْلُولَةٌ غُلَّتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَلُعِنُوا بِمَا قَالُوا بَلْ يَدَاهُ مَبْسُوطَتَانِ يُنْفِقُ كَيْفَ يَشَاءُ وَلَيَزِيدَنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنْهُمْ مَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ طُغْيَانًا وَكُفْرًا وَأَلْقَيْنَا بَيْنَهُمُ الْعَدَاوَةَ وَالْبَغْضَاءَ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ كُلَّمَا أَوْقَدُوا نَارًا لِلْحَرْبِ أَطْفَأَهَا اللَّهُ وَيَسْعَوْنَ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَسَادًا وَاللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُفْسِدِينَ) (٦٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُنْفِقُ): resumptive. It may not be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ, for two reasons. The first: that the hāʾ is a muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of a genitive construct).
The second: that the khabar (predicate) separates them. Nor may it be a ḥāl from the two hands, since there is no pronoun in it referring back to them. (لِلْحَرْبِ): it may be an adjective (ṣifa) of نار, and so attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, or it may be attached to أوقدوا. And (فَسَادًا) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

ukberi-tibyan:66-66.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ أَقَامُوا التَّوْرَاةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ لَأَكَلُوا مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ وَمِنْ تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِهِمْ مِنْهُمْ أُمَّةٌ مُقْتَصِدَةٌ وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ سَاءَ مَا يَعْمَلُونَ) (٦٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَأَكَلُوا مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ): the object of أكلوا is omitted, and من فوقهم is a naʿt (adjective) of it, its implied form being: "provision coming from above them", or "taken from above them". (سَاءَ مَا يَعْمَلُونَ): ساء here is in the sense of بئس ("how evil"), and it has been mentioned earlier.

ukberi-tibyan:67-67.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا أَيُّهَا الرَّسُولُ بَلِّغْ مَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ وَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ فَمَا بَلَّغْتَ رِسَالَتَهُ وَاللَّهُ يَعْصِمُكَ مِنَ النَّاسِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْكَافِرِينَ) (٦٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَمَا بَلَّغْتَ رِسَالَتَهُ): it is read in the singular, it being a generic noun with a plural meaning, and in the plural, because the kinds of message differ.

ukberi-tibyan:69-69.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَالَّذِينَ هَادُوا وَالصَّابِئُونَ وَالنَّصَارَى مَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ) (٦٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالصَّابِئُونَ): it is read with the hamza fully pronounced, according to the original; and with it dropped and ḍamma on the bāʾ, the original on this view being صبا, with the alif substituted for the hamza. It is also read with a yāʾ carrying ḍamma, and the reasoning is that he changed the hamza into yāʾ because of the kasra before it, and did not drop it, so as to indicate that its origin is a letter that is retained. And it is read with the hamza and in the accusative (naṣb), conjoined to الذين; this is irregular (shādhdh) in transmission but sound by analogy, and it is like the one in [Sūrat] al-Baqara. What is well known in the reading is the nominative (rafʿ), and on it there are several views. The first is the view of Sībawayh: that it is intended to come later, after the khabar (predicate) of إنّ, its implied form being: "nor shall they grieve, and the Sabians likewise"; so it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) with its khabar omitted. Similar to it is:
فَإِنَّى وَقَيَّارٌ بِهَا لَغَرِيبُ
(For I — and Qayyār too — am surely a stranger there.)
that is: "for I am surely a stranger, and Qayyār there likewise".
The second: that it is conjoined to the position of إنّ [and its noun], as in your saying إن زيدًا وعمرٌو قائمان. This is a mistake, because the khabar of إنّ is not complete: if you make قائمان the khabar of إنّ, no khabar remains for عمرو, and if you make it the khabar of عمرو, no khabar remains for إنّ. Moreover it is impossible from the point of view of meaning, because you would be giving a dual as the predicate of a singular. As for His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَمَلَائِكَتَهُ يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ), on the reading of those who put «مَلَائِكَتُهُ» in the nominative, the khabar of إنّ is omitted, its implied form being:
"Allah blesses", and the khabar of the second has made it unnecessary. Likewise, if you said إن عمرًا وزيدٌ قائم, putting زيد in the nominative, it would be permissible on the basis that it is a mubtadaʾ and قائم is its khabar, or the khabar of إنّ. The third view: that «الصَّابِئُونَ» is conjoined to the agent in هادوا. This is unsound for two reasons. The first: that it would require the Sabians to be Jews, which is not so. The second: that the pronoun has not been emphasised. The fourth view: that the khabar of الصابئين is omitted without its being intended to come later; this is also weak, because of the omission and the separation that it entails. The fifth view: that إنْ «[Translator's note: so in the text.]» is in the sense of نعم ("yes"), so what follows it is in the position of the nominative, and الصابئون likewise.
The sixth: that «الصَّابِئُونَ» is in the position of the accusative, but it has come according to the dialect of Balḥārith, who form the dual with alif in every case and the plural with wāw in every case; this is far-fetched. The seventh view: that the nūn is made the letter carrying the case ending.
If it is said: فأبوا عليّ «[Translator's note: so in the text; evidently فأبو عليّ, "Abū ʿAlī", is meant.]» allowed that only with the yāʾ, not with the wāw — it is answered: others have allowed it, and analogy does not reject it. As for «النَّصَارَى», the better view is that it is in the position of the accusative, according to the regular analogy, and no necessity calls for anything else.
